### feedback_cross_language_pitfalls.md

```markdown
---
name: Cross-language design pitfalls
description: Three approaches the user rejected when designing SoraMech's cross-language wire format
type: feedback
originSessionId: e9ed70c7-2b63-425c-987c-6431040bedfb
---
When designing anything that touches the cross-language data path, avoid these three shapes — the user pushed back on each and the rejections are load-bearing for the architecture.

**1. Don't propose runtime "handles" that route operations back to the originating spec.**

**Why:** Real library functions in the wild (qsort, libcurl, anything from libc) expect actual native values — a real `int (*)(int,int)` function pointer, a real `char *` — not a SoraMech-issued id string. They can't be modified to participate in our runtime's routing scheme. The wire must carry data the destination spec can fully reconstruct into a native value, not opaque tokens.

**How to apply:** When a value seems hard to serialize (function pointers, coroutines, opaque pointers), decompose to data primitives (address + signature, bytecode + upvalues, ptr + length). If the destination needs a callable, the destination spec synthesizes one at reconstruction time (libffi trampoline for C, `ffi.cast` for LuaJIT). The "phone home" callback that the trampoline performs internally is fine — it's an artifact of the destination spec's reconstruction, not exposed in the wire format. What's forbidden is a wire primitive that says "operations on this value cross back to the source."

**2. Don't propose pair-wise language conversion paths (lua→c, c→lua, etc.).**

**Why:** N languages means N² conversion paths, which means adding a new language breaks the existing ones. The wire must use a language-agnostic intermediate (JSON) and every spec must implement only the two pair-symmetric callbacks (`to_json`, `from_json`). New language = implement those two functions, nothing else touches.

**How to apply:** Never write code that names two specific languages in a conversion context. Specs only ever see JSON on the wire. If a JSON primitive needs an extension (like `$function_pointer`), it lives in the universal JSON contract, not as a lua-spec-specific or c-spec-specific concept.

**3. Don't propose per-function annotations for type ambiguities (lengths, discriminators, callback signatures).**

**Why:** The user pointed out that "discriminator" is a vocab word the system has no general way to ask about. We can't prompt "which param is the length?" because that pairing convention lives in the function's English documentation, not its types. Asking the user to write annotations means asking them to know specialized vocabulary they didn't sign up for.

**How to apply:** When a function signature has ambiguous types (`char *` with no length, `union` with no tag, `void *` with no signature), expose each parameter as a separate input slot on the box. The user wires the slots according to the function's documentation — `p` from one source, `n` from another. The system never infers pairings; the user expresses them by wiring. If the destination needs a length and no length wire is provided, the wire compile fails with a plain-English fix-it message ("destination needs length, source provides only a pointer — wire a length input here").

**Common thread:** all three rejections are the same principle in different clothes — **SoraMech bends to the language, not the other way around.** Users write idiomatic code in their language. Libraries are used as-is. Specs are self-contained and pair-symmetric. The system stays out of the user's vocabulary.

```

### project_cross_language_wire.md

```markdown
---
name: Cross-language wire format
description: Dual-ring slot per port (native ring + JSON ring + ordering ring). JSON only at language borders. Per-edge classification at graph load; per-cell precision at runtime.
type: project
originSessionId: 5670858b-274f-49c4-89b8-a4b83ce33d7c
---
Design corrected 2026-05-21 — replaces the older "JSON always" framing.

**Each input slot is a dual-ring buffer.** Per port: one `ring_native` (consumer-language native bytes), one `ring_json` (JSON bytes from cross-language producers), and one `ring_order` of `(which_ring, idx)` tuples in arrival order. Allocate `ring_json` and `ring_order` lazily — same-language-only ports pay nothing for them.

**Push selects ring by per-edge bit.** Producer's spec writes native bytes to `ring_native` if `output_edge_native[j]` is true; otherwise calls `native_to_json` and writes to `ring_json`. Either way, pushes a `(which_ring, idx)` tuple to `ring_order`.

**Pop reads ordering ring first.** Dispatch pops `ring_order`, gets `(which_ring, idx)`, then pops the indicated cell. The consumer's spec receives `(input_data[i], input_native[i])` per input port and dispatches per flag — decode native or decode JSON.

**Why dual-ring instead of per-port classification.** Per-port (slot is all-JSON if any fan-in is cross-lang) is the pessimistic approximation — same-language values eat JSON cost on mixed-fan-in ports. Dual-ring is precise per cell: a port fed by one Lua box and one C box keeps the Lua cells native and JSON-encodes only the C-sourced cells.

**Why JSON for the cross-language ring (not pair-wise paths, not type-annotated raw bytes).** JSON's structure is self-describing — every language has a natural mapping for object/array/number/string/bool/null. Adding language K means K's spec implements its own `native_to_json` and `json_to_native`. N spec-pairs, not N² language-pair paths. The native ring's format is each spec's private choice — Lua may pick msgpack or `cjson.encode` or a custom binary form; C uses `memcpy` of the wrapper struct; Bash uses strings.

**Sentinel primitives for non-JSON-mappable values.** `$ref` (pointer + length into the large-value heap), `$function_pointer`, `$lang_opaque` ("these bytes are language-X-internal"). Carried inside the JSON ring as object-shaped sentinels. Cross-language receivers that can't reconstruct fail at wire compile.

**`$function_pointer` reconstruction — wrapper binary + persistent subprocess (issue 318, amended 2026-05-22).** Earlier design had the consumer's spec FFI-cast the raw process-local address. Rejected: FFI is language-pair-specific, biases SoraMech toward the Lua↔C corner, breaks the N-not-N² rule. Replacement: at map-compile time the compiler asks the *producing* spec to compile the referenced function + its enumerable dependencies into a standalone wrapper binary on disk that speaks a small line protocol on stdio. The consumer spec spawns one persistent subprocess per `$function_pointer` it receives and talks to it over the same socket-like channel used for any out-of-process spec. Every language pays the same price; new languages only implement "compile a function to a wrapper binary" — no pair-wise FFI knowledge required.

**Spec `invoke` signature change.** Collapses `invoke_native` and `invoke_json` into one `invoke` with per-input/per-output flags: `int invoke(handle, ..., const int *input_native, int n_inputs, int output_native, void *out_buf, ...)`. The spec dispatches per input internally. This is the contract change that unblocks 306/307's typed marshalling.

**Two compile-time layers stack:**
- **Per-edge classification (issue 312, this design)** — graph loader computes `input_edge_native[]` and `output_edge_native[]` on each box; dispatch routes pushes accordingly. This issue is the wire-format design.
- **Same-language source merge (issue 313, research / blocked)** — concatenate every same-language box's source into one translation unit per language. Boxes still run as separate thread-pool tasks; what 313 thins is the spec invocation overhead inside the merged region (direct call into the worker's `lua_State` instead of dlsym + marshal + bridge). The dual-ring slot machinery does NOT collapse — tasks still need slots to wait for sibling inputs. 313 makes the ring cells cheaper to read/write; it doesn't remove them.

**Three rejected design shapes** (kept here so they don't get reinvented):
1. **Handles back-routing to the owning spec** — library functions in the wild can't be modified to use SoraMech-shaped handles. Rejected.
2. **Pair-wise language paths** — every new language would have to grow N-1 translation paths against existing languages. Rejected. The dual-ring's "two rings per slot" is the dimension-cap that prevents this.
3. **Per-function discriminator / length annotations on the wire** — the system has no universal vocabulary to ask "is param 2 the length?" Rejected; the user expresses these by wiring two separate input slots.

**How to apply:** When discussing wire format, slot store shape, dispatch routing, or spec callbacks: think dual-ring (native, JSON, ordering) per slot, per-edge classification at push time, per-cell tag at pop time, JSON-only-at-borders, language-private native bytes everywhere else.

```

### project_custom_translation_specs.md

```markdown
---
name: Custom translation specs per port
description: Users can override the default native/JSON wire path on any input port for any reason — a knob in the wire format vocabulary (issue 246)
type: project
originSessionId: 1228a221-1c09-4c26-94f3-172d7777b2b9
---
**Per-port custom translation specs** let the user intervene at a specific input port and replace the default dual-ring decode path with user-written code. The override applies to that one port; the rest of the graph uses the default native-or-JSON path from issue 312.

**Motivating cases (any reason qualifies, not just cross-language):**
- Cross-language ambiguity the default specs can't infer: a C++ class with methods landing at a C box (drop methods? expose as fn pointers? restructure?), a `void *` carrying a libcurl handle, a union whose discriminator is on a separate wire.
- Same-language reshape: massaging a value into a different shape on its way in (rename fields, drop a layer, project a subset) without adding a transform box on the canvas.
- Validation / coercion: clamp a number, enforce a schema, fail loudly on unexpected shapes.

**How it composes with the dual-ring design:**
- The custom spec runs at *pop* time on the consumer side, after the ordering ring has been consulted and the cell has been read from the appropriate ring. The user's code receives the decoded value (native or JSON-decoded) and produces whatever the consumer's `invoke` will see.
- A port with a custom translation gets its own wire color in the editor (issue 245) — visible signal that this port doesn't use the default path.

**Why:** The default native/JSON contract covers the cases JSON's structure handles cleanly. Everything outside that needs a user escape hatch — *and* the same hatch is useful for purely-local "I want this input shaped differently" cases. One mechanism, many uses.

**How to apply:** When the design needs an override knob on the cross-language path, propose "custom translation spec on the destination port" rather than inventing per-function annotations, type discriminator metadata, or producer-side conversion hints (all three were rejected — see feedback_cross_language_pitfalls). The port is the unit of override; the spec is user code; the rest stays default.

```

### project_editor_visual_language.md

```markdown
---
name: Editor visual language for wires
description: Wire color in the canvas editor encodes language pairing across the edge, not just routing kind — a UI invariant future work should respect (issue 245)
type: project
originSessionId: 1228a221-1c09-4c26-94f3-172d7777b2b9
---
**Wires are colored by language pairing across the edge**, with a separate color for wires whose destination port carries a user-written custom translation (issue 246). Pre-245 wires were colored purely by routing kind (default slate-blue, comparator branches orange/blue/green).

**The pairing-based palette:**
- **Same-language hop** — the wire carries native bytes; default neutral color.
- **Cross-language hop (forest green, ~`#228b22`)** — different producer/consumer languages; runtime translates via JSON at the wire. The color is a standing reminder that encode + decode is happening on that hop.
- **Custom-translation hop** — a third distinct color signaling the destination port has a user-written translation spec overriding the default path.
- Branch-routing colors (orange/blue/green from comparator boxes) compose on top — routing kind and language pairing are orthogonal axes the editor must show simultaneously.

**Why:** The runtime treats same-lang and cross-lang hops very differently (dual-ring slot design, issue 312), but pre-245 the editor gave the box author no visual signal that the JSON translation step existed. It was invisible until someone read the dispatch code. Translation cost should be legible from the canvas.

**How to apply:** Any future editor work that touches wire rendering must preserve "color encodes language pairing." Don't propose recoloring schemes that overload the cross-language signal onto another concept. New routing concepts get new axes (line style, glyphs, animation) rather than stealing color. When discussing wire visuals, name both axes — routing kind AND language pairing — even if only one is changing.

```

### project_encapsulated_map.md

```markdown
---
name: Encapsulated map as box
description: A sub-map opens as a single box on a parent canvas. Data boxes marked externally-supplied become input ports; write boxes marked externally-consumed become output ports. The documented exception to single-output-per-box (issue 248, amended 2026-05-23)
type: project
originSessionId: 1228a221-1c09-4c26-94f3-172d7777b2b9
---
**A map directory has two ways to be opened:** as the top-level graph (existing map-select UI), or as an **encapsulated box** on the currently-edited parent map (issue 248). Opening through the file browser while a parent map is open instantiates the sub-map as a single box on the parent's canvas.

**The encapsulation contract — symmetric input and output toggles:**
- **Inputs:** any `data` box inside the sub-map can be toggled "externally-supplied" in its inspector. Each such box becomes a typed input port on the encapsulated box.
- **Outputs:** any `write` box inside the sub-map can be toggled "externally-consumed" in its inspector. Each such box surfaces as a **distinct output port** on the encapsulated box. A write box with the toggle on can still write to its `path` if one is set — the file destination and the parent-wire destination are independent.

**Encapsulated maps are the documented exception to issue 218's "single output per box" rule.** They have *N* output ports — one per externally-consumed write box, where *N* may be zero (pure side-effect map), one, or many. Every other box kind still has exactly one output.

**Rejected earlier design (2026-05-21):** packing all write-box outputs into a single byte-blob with a leading null-terminated size index, single wire out. Rejected 2026-05-23 because it would have repurposed file-writing machinery to emit strings into wires — substituting one mechanism for another. The symmetric toggle design preserves the `write` box's "terminate a value" semantics and treats the destination kind as a mode toggle.

**Why:** Encapsulation is a function-like abstraction over a sub-graph. The parent doesn't see the sub-map's internals — it sees declared input ports, declared output ports, and known semantics. Sub-maps can be edited independently, reused across parents, and packaged once for distribution. This is the closest SoraMech gets to "user-defined functions" while staying graph-native.

**How to apply:** When discussing map composition, reuse, or "how do users build libraries of behavior" — encapsulation is the answer. Don't propose alternative function-abstraction mechanisms (named subgraphs as text references, macro-style inlining, blob-packed outputs) without explicitly weighing them against the symmetric-toggle shape. Both toggles (`externally-supplied` on data boxes, `externally-consumed` on write boxes) are the user-facing port-declaration mechanism — don't invent a separate "ports manifest" file.

```

### project_soramech.md

```markdown
---
name: SoraMech project context
description: Core architecture decisions, file layout, and execution model for SoraMech, across phase 2 (current) and phase 3 (designed)
type: project
originSessionId: 579d58b3-7452-44f3-983a-80ff5821082a
---
SoraMech is a visual FSM/dataflow editor and execution engine at /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/.

**Why:** Primary use case is LLM orchestration on the SoraMind Alpine cluster. Strings flow between boxes like variables. History is explicit, loaded from disk only when a box needs it.

**Three independent programs sharing a map directory:**
- `src/006-server-main.lua` — thin HTTP file CRUD proxy. No runner management.
- Runner — phase 2: `src/007-runner-main.lua` (synchronous Lua). Phase 3: `soramech-pool` (C binary, designed in issues 301–311, not yet built).
- `assets/index.html` — vanilla JS canvas editor. Editor only — no run button. Compile button (issue 222) is a phase 2 placeholder; it triggers the phase 3 build pipeline (issue 219).

**Key architecture decisions (current truth):**
- Each box is its own JSON file in `boxes/<id>.json`. Connections written to BOTH endpoint files; loader validates both ends agree — hard error if not.
- **Single output wire per box** (issue 218 complete). No `outputs` array. The function returns one value; routing is by `from_branch` on the connection.
- **Comparator-based branching** (issue 210) — replaces the earlier `branch` box kind with named ports. A box may carry a `comparand`; the dispatch layer fires `lt`/`eq`/`gt` connections. No spec is invoked for comparators.
- **Iterator boxes** (issue 221) — pure routing primitives, no `ref`/`fn`. Dispatch layer cycles through `iterator_outputs` based on a per-task counter.
- **Phase 2 drivers** are shell scripts under `drivers/` (one process per call, stdout as channel). **Phase 3 language specs** are `.so` libraries under `langs/<name>/spec.so` loaded via `dlopen` (issue 303). Lua and C are in-process; Bash is out-of-process via Unix domain socket.
- Data files: per-map JSON in `data/`. Section-level `constant` flag. Accessed via `libs/soramech-data.lua`.
- State/ephemeral: `tmp/` is a symlink to `/tmp/<map-name>/`. Phase 2 writes `last-run.json` (single doc). Phase 3 writes `last-run.jsonl` (JSON Lines, issue 311) — decoupled from the editor, consumed by LLMs / CLI viewers / test harness.
- **Phase 3 runtime model**: C pool runner owns a 3d-rts task pool; per-task slots in process heap (issue 302) with refcounting and a separate large-value heap; dispatch layer (304) is the worker action; graph loader is C (305), no embedded Lua at the runner level. Phase 2's synchronous executor retires when phase 3 lands.

**How to apply:** When working on any component, respect the three-way separation. Server never knows about runner. Runner never knows about server. Map directory format is the only shared contract. The phase 2 driver model and the phase 3 spec model coexist conceptually (phase 2 is current, phase 3 is fully designed) but the runtime mechanism differs entirely; box JSON and the editor are unchanged across the cutover.

```

### project_threading.md

```markdown
---
name: threading_model
description: SoraMech's threading model — phase 2 synchronous, phase 3 SoraMech-owned C thread pool with per-port slots and language specs
type: project
originSessionId: 579d58b3-7452-44f3-983a-80ff5821082a
---
**Phase 2 (current)**: synchronous executor in `src/004-executor.lua`. Single-threaded, sequential box execution. One driver shell-out per box call. The phase 2 path goes away when phase 3 lands — no fallback, no coroutine intermediate.

**Phase 3 (designed, not yet built)**: C pool runner with a SoraMech-owned thread pool. The 3d-rts pool at `/home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/games/3d-rts/libs/900-task-pool.h` is the **design reference**, not vendored — SoraMech owns its pool implementation so the spawn primitive, worker context, init barrier, and iterator-pinning extensions are all under our control. The architecture is fully specified across issues 301–313.

Key phase 3 concepts:
- **Per-input-port slots** (not per-task), allocated at graph load and durable for the run. Each slot is a ring buffer (`n_cells` cells of `cell_capacity` bytes). 1-cell slots use peek-not-drain (literals, single-push wires); N-cell slots use pop-and-drain (queued / multi-push wires). No per-slot refcounting — slot lifetime is the whole run.
- **Tasks are ephemeral**: spawned dynamically by the dispatch layer when a box's input set is ready. Tasks carry just `box_id` and a counter snapshot. Box state (counter, input slots, language handle) is durable.
- **Language specs** under `langs/<name>/spec.so`, loaded via `dlopen` at startup. Uniform `lang_spec_t`. No language is privileged.
- **Same-language fast path** (issue 312): wire format defaults to JSON, but two adjacent same-language boxes use the language's native serialization (Lua `lua_dump`, C struct memcpy). Compile-time wire classification picks the path.
- **In-process specs** (Lua, C) via `lua_pcall` / `dlsym`. **Out-of-process specs** (Bash) via Unix domain sockets to a persistent per-worker subprocess.
- **Dispatch layer** (304) is the worker-side action: pop inputs → branch on box mode → invoke spec → push to downstream input slots → end. No blocking, no wait lists; tasks spawn on input arrival and run to completion.
- **Iterator and comparator routing** in the dispatch layer. Comparator runs the function and routes by output value. Iterator skips the function and routes by per-box counter (atomic spawn-time increment). Iterator tasks parallelize across workers; ordering preserved via per-push counter tags on consumer slots.
- **No-null rule** (issue 230): every input port must be wired, given a literal, or marked optional. Compile fails on missing inputs.
- **Init barrier**: pool startup waits until every worker has run every spec's `init(worker_idx)` before submitting tasks. Avoids tasks landing on uninitialized handles.
- **Hard-crash error policy**: nonzero return from any spec aborts the program.
- **Blocking semantics**: long-running operations tie up a worker. Pool size is the budget. Cooperative split (kickoff + check-done iterator) avoids holding a worker. See `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md`.

**Effil is explicitly NOT used.** Coroutines are not used. The C pool is the chosen mechanism. 3d-rts is referenced as design inspiration, not vendored.

**How to apply:** When discussing threading, parallelism, or cross-language IPC: phase 2 is synchronous shell-out drivers; phase 3 is the SoraMech-owned C pool runner with `lang_spec_t`, per-port slot stores, and dispatch-layer routing. Never suggest effil. 3d-rts is a reference, not a dependency. Issues 301–313 carry the design.

```

        "content":"1\t# 305 — C graph loader (replaces 003-loader.lua)\n2\t\n3\t## Status\n4\topen\n5\t\n6\t## Current behavior\n7\tThe phase 2 loader at `src/003-loader.lua` reads a map directory's\n8\t`boxes/*.json`, `data/*.json`, and metadata, decodes JSON via dkjson,\n9\truns schema validation, builds the in-memory graph table, and detects\n10\tentry boxes. It is Lua. The synchronous executor consumes its output.\n11\t\n12\tThe phase 3 pool runner (issue 301) cannot embed a Lua state for\n13\tloading — Lua appears in the runner only as a per-box language runtime,\n14\tnever as the runner's own scripting layer. The loader is therefore\n15\tported to C and lives inside (or alongside) `src/008-pool-runner.c`.\n16\t\n17\t## Concept\n18\t\n19\tThe C graph loader is the first phase of the pool runner's startup. It:\n20\t1. Walks the map directory.\n21\t2. Parses every JSON file.\n22\t3. Validates schema and connection topology.\n23\t4. Builds a single `graph_t` struct that the pool runner and dispatch\n24\t   layer consume.\n25\t\n26\tThe loader is a one-shot at startup. It crashes the program on any\n27\tvalidation failure (per the hard-crash policy in issue 303). There is\n28\tno recovery, no skip-bad-boxes mode.\n29\t\n30\t## Inputs\n31\t\n32\tThe map directory layout (unchanged from phase 2):\n33\t\n34\t```\n35\tmaps/<name>/\n36\t    meta.json          ← entry box, src_dirs, run-level metadata\n37\t    boxes/*.json       ← one file per box\n38\t    data/*.json        ← static data values (literal inputs)\n39\t    src/*              ← box function source files (resolved via meta.src_dirs)\n40\t```\n41\t\n42\tThe loader is given the map directory path as a C string.\n43\t\n44\t## Output: `graph_t`\n45\t\n46\t```c\n47\ttypedef struct {\n48\t    int           n_boxes;\n49\t    box_t        *boxes;            // array of box descriptors\n50\t    int           n_connections;\n51\t    connection_t *connections;\n52\t    int           n_size_classes;\n53\t    int          *size_classes;     // distinct slot sizes the graph uses\n54\t    int           n_entry_boxes;\n55\t    int          *entry_box_ids;    // indices into boxes[]\n56\t    int           n_languages;\n57\t    const char  **languages;        // distinct language names used\n58\t} graph_t;\n59\t\n60\ttypedef struct {\n61\t    char         *id;               // user-defined box id (\"classifier\", \"stamp\", …)\n62\t    char         *kind;             // \"call\" | \"data\"\n63\t    char         *lang;             // \"lua\" | \"c\" | \"bash\" | ...; NULL for data and iterator/comparator\n64\t    char         *ref;               // file path; NULL for data/iterator/comparator\n65\t    char         *fn;                // function name; NULL for data/iterator/comparator\n66\t    int           n_inputs;\n67\t    input_decl_t *inputs;\n68\t    int           output_capacity;  // bytes; 0 if variable-size (uses large-value heap)\n69\t    int           is_comparator;\n70\t    int           is_iterator;\n71\t    int           n_iter_outputs;\n72\t    char        **iter_output_names;\n73\t    // …\n74\t} box_t;\n75\t\n76\ttypedef struct {\n77\t    int   from_box_id;\n78\t    char *from_branch;              // NULL for plain call; \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\" for comparator;\n79\t                                    // iterator output name otherwise\n80\t    int   to_box_id;\n81\t    char *to_input_name;\n82\t    int   to_input_index;\n83\t} connection_t;\n84\t```\n85\t\n86\tStrings are owned by the graph (allocated from a single arena attached\n87\tto the graph; freed when the graph is destroyed at the end of the run).\n88\t\n89\t## Loading phases\n90\t\n91\t### 1. Directory walk\n92\tOpen the map directory, enumerate `boxes/`, `data/`, and the optional\n93\t`meta.json`. Each entry is queued for parsing.\n94\t\n95\t### 2. JSON parse\n96\tUse the vendored JSON parser (issue 301 lists cJSON / jsmn / hand-rolled\n97\tas candidates). Each file becomes a parsed JSON tree. Parse errors are\n98\tfatal — print the file path and the parser's error message, abort.\n99\t\n100\t### 3. Schema validation\n101\tBox kinds and what they mean at runtime:\n102\t\n103\t- **`call`** is a verb — a box that runs a function (or, for iterator\n104\t  and comparator variants, a dispatch-layer routing primitive). Each\n105\t  call box becomes a `dispatch_task_t` in the pool when its inputs\n106\t  are ready.\n107\t- **`data`** is a noun — a literal value embedded in the map. It has\n108\t  no function and produces no task in the pool. Its output slot is\n109\t  allocated and filled at startup by the loader and remains filled\n110\t  for the duration of the run; downstream consumers read it like any\n111\t  other slot.\n112\t\n113\tRequired fields per kind:\n114\t- `id`, `kind` always required.\n115\t- For `kind == \"call\"`: either (a) `lang`, `ref`, `fn` (plain call\n116\t  box), or (b) `iterator_outputs` (iterator box, no `ref`/`fn`), or\n117\t  (c) `comparator` field set (comparator box, no `ref`/`fn`).\n118\t- For `kind == \"data\"`: a `value` field; no `inputs` or `connections`\n119\t  (other than outgoing wires from this box's output slot).\n120\t\n121\tBox ids must be unique across the map. Connection endpoints must\n122\treference valid box ids and valid input names.\n123\t\n124\tSchema rules mirror `src/001-schema.lua`. The C validator is a port of\n125\tthat file's logic, simplified by the absence of port-named branching\n126\t(removed in issue 108 cleanup).\n127\t\n128\t### 4. Topology validation\n129\t- Every connection's `from_box` and `to_box` exist.\n130\t- Every connection's `to_input_name` matches a declared input on the\n131\t  destination box.\n132\t- No non-iterator cycles. The validator runs DFS; any cycle that does\n133\t  not pass through an iterator box is rejected.\n134\t- Every required input has at least one connection feeding it (or is\n135\t  fed by a `data` box).\n136\t\n137\tValidation failure aborts the program with a precise error message —\n138\twhich box, which connection, what was wrong.\n139\t\n140\t### 5. Slot size class enumeration\n141\tWalk every box and queued-input declaration to enumerate the distinct\n142\tslot sizes the graph will need. Each unique size becomes a size class\n143\tin the slot allocator (issue 302). Output:\n144\t\n145\t```c\n146\tgraph->size_classes      = { 64, 256, 1024, 65536 };  // example\n147\tgraph->n_size_classes    = 4;\n148\t```\n149\t\n150\tThe slot allocator pre-populates each class's free list with\n151\t`n_workers × (count of boxes whose output is this size)` slots. This\n152\tcovers the worst case — every worker concurrently producing an output\n153\tat this size class — without overshooting. Demand beyond this triggers\n154\tgrowth (issue 302); the per-thread multiplier is the right ceiling for\n155\tthe static count, while leaving headroom for iterators that allocate\n156\tper-invocation slots.\n157\t\n158\t### 6. Entry-box detection\n159\tA box is an entry box if either:\n160\t- It has zero inputs, or\n161\t- All of its inputs are connected only to `data` boxes (literal values\n162\t  with no upstream computation).\n163\t\n164\tEntry boxes are submitted to the pool first; everything else fires from\n165\tpost-action routing in the dispatch layer.\n166\t\n167\tA map can have any number of entry boxes. The user lays out the\n168\tinitial program state via `data` boxes and entry-point call boxes; the\n169\trunner submits all entries at once, and the graph propagates from\n170\tthere. There is no singular `main`.\n171\t\n172\t### 7. Language enumeration\n173\tCollect the distinct `lang` values across all plain call boxes. The\n174\tpool runner uses this set to decide which language specs (issue 303)\n175\tto load and which per-worker handles to initialize.\n176\t\n177\tIterator and comparator boxes have no `lang` and contribute nothing\n178\there.\n179\t\n180\t### Note on built-in primitives vs shipped libraries\n181\t\n182\tThere are two distinct categories of \"things the user gets out of the\n183\tbox,\" and they live in different places:\n184\t\n185\t- **Dispatch-layer primitives** are graph-topology operations whose\n186\t  semantics are routing, not data transformation. Iterator and\n187\t  comparator are the two so far. They have no `lang` / `ref` / `fn` —\n188\t  the dispatch layer implements their behavior directly. Splitter\n189\t  / fan-out is already free via wire fan-out and does not need its\n190\t  own box kind. Possible future primitives: a \"gate\" (forward only\n191\t  when a control input is truthy), a \"merge\" (forward whichever\n192\t  input arrives first). These are not on the roadmap; flagged here\n193\t  so the door stays open.\n194\t- **Shipped libraries** are data-transformation utilities — JSON\n195\t  parse/serialize, file read/write, string concat/split, regex,\n196\t  shell-out. These are language-specific (string semantics differ\n197\t  between Lua, C, and Bash) and ship as `libs/<name>.<ext>` per\n198\t  language. They are not built into the dispatch layer; they are\n199\t  ordinary call-box source files that users wire into their maps.\n200\t  `libs/ollama.lua` is an existing example.\n201\t\n202\tThe distinction matters: dispatch-layer primitives change the graph\n203\tmodel; shipped libraries don't. A dispatch primitive can do things a\n204\tfunction call cannot (like routing on a counter); a library is just\n205\tcode that happens to be vendored.\n206\t\n207\t## Error policy\n208\t\n209\tAny failure in any phase aborts the program. The loader prints:\n210\t- The map path\n211\t- The phase that failed (parse / schema / topology / etc.)\n212\t- The specific file or box that caused the failure\n213\t- The parser's or validator's diagnostic message\n214\t\n215\tThen `exit(1)`. There is no partial-load mode.\n216\t\n217\t## Open questions\n218\t\n219\t- JSON library choice: cJSON (heaviest, easiest, well-maintained),\n220\t  jsmn (tiny, no allocations, manual tree walking), or hand-rolled\n221\t  (smallest dependency footprint, more code). Decision deferred to\n222\t  implementation time.\n223\t### String storage\n224\t\n225\tA \"string arena\" is a single `malloc`-backed buffer the graph loader\n226\tuses to store every string it owns (box ids, file paths, function\n227\tnames, branch tags) packed end-to-end. Each string is a `char *`\n228\tpointing into the arena. Allocating a string is just bumping the\n229\tarena's offset; freeing happens once when the arena is destroyed at\n230\tthe end of the run, in a single `free(arena_buffer)`.\n231\t\n232\tThis is faster and simpler than calling `malloc` per string: one\n233\t`free` for thousands of strings, no fragmentation, and lookup is\n234\tjust a pointer.\n235\t\n236\tThe arena starts small and grows on demand by `realloc`-ing to a\n237\tlarger size when the current buffer fills up. Because every stored\n238\tstring is referenced by a `char *` into the arena, a `realloc` that\n239\tmoves the buffer would invalidate all the pointers — so the loader\n240\teither uses a series of fixed-size chunks (a chunk list rather than a\n241\tsingle growable buffer) or pre-sizes the arena from the file count\n242\tto avoid mid-load realloc. Chunk-list is the standard answer.\n243\t\n244\t## Suggested implementation sequence\n245\t\n246\t1. Vendor the chosen JSON parser into `libs/json/`.\n247\t2. Output should match\n257\t   the box outputs declared in `maps/hello` and `maps/classify-demo`.\n258\t7. Implement phases 6 (entry boxes) and 7 (languages). Verify against\n259\t   known maps.\n260\t8. Wire the loader into `src/008-pool-runner.c`'s `main` so the pool\n261\t   runner starts by loading and validating before doing anything\n262\t   else.\n263\t\n264\t## Relevant files\n265\t\n266\t- `src/003-loader.lua` — phase 2 loader, ported by this issue\n267\t- `src/001-schema.lua` — phase 2 schema validator, also ported\n268\t- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — pool runner that owns and uses the loader\n269\t- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool lifecycle that\n270\t  consumes the graph\n271\t- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — slot allocator that consumes\n272\t  the size class list\n273\t- `issues/303-language-runtime-spec.md` — spec registry that consumes\n274\t  the language list\n275\t- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch layer that consumes\n276\t  the box and connection arrays\n277\t- `issues/219-map-compiler.md` — the compiler is the other consumer of\n278\t  the same validation logic; the C loader and the compiler should\n279\t  share validation code if possible\n280\t\n281\t## Implementation log\n282\t\n283\t### Phase 1 + 2 + early phase 3 — 2026-05-12\n284\t\n285\tWhat shipped:\n286\t- `src/010-graph-loader.h` — public types and API. `graph_t` is\n287\t  opaque; the box / connection / input declaration shapes are\n288\t  public so the dispatch layer (issue 304) can walk them directly.\n289\t  Routing kinds align with issue 233 — `routing_t` with `kind`\n290\t  plus per-kind parameters, no legacy `comparand` /\n291\t  `iterator_outputs` top-level fields.\n292\t- `src/010-graph-loader.c` — implementation. Pipeline: open the\n293\t  map dir, parse `meta.json` via the project JSON parser\n294\t  (issue 314), walk every `.json` under `boxes/`, parse each into\n295\t  a `box_t`, enforce kind-specific required fields (ref/routing\n296\t  for call; path for data; inputs only for file_write), validate\n297\t  id uniqueness across boxes. Errors return a malloc'd\n298\t  `<file>:<line>: <message>` diagnostic via the `**err`\n299\t  out-parameter; the pool runner's main is expected to print and\n300\t  abort.\n301\t- `tests/maps/hello/` and `tests/maps/branching/` — fixture maps\n302\t  exercising the call/data combo, comparator routing (lt/eq/gt\n303\t  branches all present), and iterator routing (n_outputs=3).\n304\t- `tests/010-graph-loader-test.c` — 7 unit tests covering\n305\t  successful loads of both fixtures, missing map directory,\n306\t  NULL argument, unknown box kind, missing routing, and\n307\t  duplicate box id. Malformed-shape tests use mkdtemp scratch\n308\t  dirs so the tracked fixtures stay valid.\n309\t- Memory model: one `json_arena_t` per loaded graph holds every\n310\t  string and every parsed tree from every file; the box,\n311\t  connection, and input declaration arrays are plain malloc.\n312\t  `graph_destroy` releases all of it.\n313\t- `.gitignore` anchored to `/maps/` so `tests/maps/` is tracked.\n314\t- Makefile per-test dependency line for `010-graph-loader-test`\n315\t  linking the loader and the JSON parser.\n316\t\n317\tVerified `make STRICT=1` builds cleanly; 33 tests across three\n318\tsuites (slot store 12, graph loader 7, JSON 14) all pass.\n319\t\n320\tWhat's deferred to follow-on iterations within 305:\n321\t- **Phase 4 — topology validation.** Connection endpoints store\n322\t  string refs only. The next pass resolves `to_box` to integer\n323\t  indices, verifies endpoints exist, and detects non-iterator\n324\t  cycles via DFS.\n325\t- **Phase 5 — slot size class enumeration.** The loader needs to\n326\t  walk every box output and produce the distinct `cell_capacity`\n327\t  values the slot store's allocator pre-populates.\n328\t- **Phase 6 — entry-box detection.** A box with zero inputs or\n329\t  with all inputs fed only by `data` boxes is an entry. The pool\n330\t  runner spawns initial tasks for these.\n331\t- **Phase 7 — language enumeration.** Distinct `lang` values\n332\t  across call boxes, handed to the spec registry (issue 303).\n333\t- The remaining routing kinds from issue 233 (randomizer,\n334\t  weighted, distributor) — the parser currently rejects them with\n335\t  a precise message.\n336\t\n337\tNone of those block 301 / 303 / 306. Topology and language\n338\tenumeration land before 304 (the dispatch layer) since the\n339\tdispatch action needs both.\n340\t\n341\t### Topology endpoint resolution — 2026-05-12\n342\t\n343\tAfter `load_boxes` succeeds, a `resolve_topology` pass walks every\n344\toutgoing connection on every box and resolves the `to_box` string\n345\tto its index in `graph->boxes`, and `to_input` to its index in\n346\tthe target box's `inputs[]`. Both string refs are preserved on\n347\t`connection_t` for diagnostics. Misses surface as\n348\t`box 'X' has a connection to nonexistent box 'Y'` or\n349\t`... nonexistent input 'Z'`. The `branching` fixture grew three more box\n352\tfiles (`small`, `exact`, `big`) so its three comparator branches\n353\thave real targets now.\n354\t\n355\tStill deferred within 305: slot size class enumeration, entry-box\n356\tdetection, language enumeration.\n357\t\n358\t### Non-iterator cycle detection — 2026-05-12\n359\t\n360\tStandard DFS with white/gray/black coloring; the only twist is\n361\tthat we skip outgoing edges from iterator-routing boxes, since\n362\tcycles passing through an iterator are legitimate (the iterator's\n363\tinput queue eventually empties and the loop terminates). Two new\n364\tfixture-based tests cover the reject case (`a → b → a`, no\n365\titerator) and the allowed case (`a → iter → b → a`).\n366\t\n367\t### Runtime attach (slot allocation + spec resolution) — 2026-05-12\n368\t\n369\t`graph_attach_runtime(g, slots, specs, default_cell_bytes, err)`\n370\twalks every box and:\n371\t- allocates one 1-cell peek slot per declared input port via\n372\t  `slot_alloc`, storing the slot id in `box->input_slot_ids[i]`;\n373\t- resolves the spec for each call box by looking up `box->lang`\n374\t  in the registry (or, as a fallback, by matching the file\n375\t  extension of `box->ref`), storing the result on\n376\t  `box->spec_idx`.\n377\t\n378\tThe graph also remembers its `map_dir` so the dispatch layer can\n379\tresolve relative paths for data boxes and file_write boxes.\n380\t\n381\tWhat's still deferred:\n382\t- **Language enumeration on the graph.** We resolve per-box but\n383\t  don't expose the distinct set of languages a map uses, so\n384\t  workers init every spec rather than only the ones in use.\n385\t\n386\t### Per-input slot modes + multi-spawn propagation — 2026-05-12\n387\t\n388\t`graph_attach_runtime` now picks the slot mode per input port:\n389\t- A new BFS pass (`propagate_multi_spawn`) seeds every iterator-\n390\t  routing call box as `multi_spawn = 1` and propagates the flag\n391\t  forward through the connection graph. Every box reachable from\n392\t  an iterator is now flagged.\n393\t- For multi-spawn boxes, each input slot is allocated as a\n394\t  16-cell pop ring. For single-spawn boxes, the legacy 1-cell\n395\t  peek slot is used.\n396\t- `box->input_slot_modes[]` carries the per-port mode\n397\t  (`SLOT_MODE_PEEK` / `SLOT_MODE_POP`) so the dispatch action\n398\t  picks the right read op.\n399\t\n400\tThis is the compile-time wire classification the architecture\n401\tdoc described, with a single-step forward propagation rule. A\n402\tproper per-wire classification (an iterator-rooted wire is\n403\tmulti-push regardless of the immediate consumer's status) would\n404\tallow finer-grained mode picks; the current rule is conservative\n405\tin the right direction (slots that *could* be POP are POP).\n406\t",

      "content":"# 305 — C graph loader (replaces 003-loader.lua)\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nThe phase 2 loader at `src/003-loader.lua` reads a map directory's\n`boxes/*.json`, `data/*.json`, and metadata, decodes JSON via dkjson,\nruns schema validation, builds the in-memory graph table, and detects\nentry boxes. It is Lua. The synchronous executor consumes its output.\n\nThe phase 3 pool runner (issue 301) cannot embed a Lua state for\nloading — Lua appears in the runner only as a per-box language runtime,\nnever as the runner's own scripting layer. The loader is therefore\nported to C and lives inside (or alongside) `src/008-pool-runner.c`.\n\n## Concept\n\nThe C graph loader is the first phase of the pool runner's startup. It:\n1. Walks the map directory.\n2. Parses every JSON file.\n3. Validates schema and connection topology.\n4. Builds a single `graph_t` struct that the pool runner and dispatch\n   layer consume.\n\nThe loader is a one-shot at startup. It crashes the program on any\nvalidation failure (per the hard-crash policy in issue 303). There is\nno recovery, no skip-bad-boxes mode.\n\n## Inputs\n\nThe map directory layout (unchanged from phase 2):\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/\n    meta.json          ← entry box, src_dirs, run-level metadata\n    boxes/*.json       ← one file per box\n    data/*.json        ← static data values (literal inputs)\n    src/*              ← box function source files (resolved via meta.src_dirs)\n```\n\nThe loader is given the map directory path as a C string.\n\n## Output: `graph_t`\n\n```c\ntypedef struct {\n    int           n_boxes;\n    box_t        *boxes;            // array of box descriptors\n    int           n_connections;\n    connection_t *connections;\n    int           n_size_classes;\n    int          *size_classes;     // distinct slot sizes the graph uses\n    int           n_entry_boxes;\n    int          *entry_box_ids;    // indices into boxes[]\n    int           n_languages;\n    const char  **languages;        // distinct language names used\n} graph_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    char         *id;               // user-defined box id (\"classifier\", \"stamp\", …)\n    char         *kind;             // \"call\" | \"data\"\n    char         *lang;             // \"lua\" | \"c\" | \"bash\" | ...; NULL for data and iterator/comparator\n    char         *ref;               // file path; NULL for data/iterator/comparator\n    char         *fn;                // function name; NULL for data/iterator/comparator\n    int           n_inputs;\n    input_decl_t *inputs;\n    int           output_capacity;  // bytes; 0 if variable-size (uses large-value heap)\n    int           is_comparator;\n    int           is_iterator;\n    int           n_iter_outputs;\n    char        **iter_output_names;\n    // …\n} box_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    int   from_box_id;\n    char *from_branch;              // NULL for plain call; \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\" for comparator;\n                                    // iterator output name otherwise\n    int   to_box_id;\n    char *to_input_name;\n    int   to_input_index;\n} connection_t;\n```\n\nStrings are owned by the graph (allocated from a single arena attached\nto the graph; freed when the graph is destroyed at the end of the run).\n\n## Loading phases\n\n### 1. Directory walk\nOpen the map directory, enumerate `boxes/`, `data/`, and the optional\n`meta.json`. Each entry is queued for parsing.\n\n### 2. JSON parse\nUse the vendored JSON parser (issue 301 lists cJSON / jsmn / hand-rolled\nas candidates). Each file becomes a parsed JSON tree. Parse errors are\nfatal — print the file path and the parser's error message, abort.\n\n### 3. Schema validation\nBox kinds and what they mean at runtime:\n\n- **`call`** is a verb — a box that runs a function (or, for iterator\n  and comparator variants, a dispatch-layer routing primitive). Each\n  call box becomes a `dispatch_task_t` in the pool when its inputs\n  are ready.\n- **`data`** is a noun — a literal value embedded in the map. It has\n  no function and produces no task in the pool. Its output slot is\n  allocated and filled at startup by the loader and remains filled\n  for the duration of the run; downstream consumers read it like any\n  other slot.\n\nRequired fields per kind:\n- `id`, `kind` always required.\n- For `kind == \"call\"`: either (a) `lang`, `ref`, `fn` (plain call\n  box), or (b) `iterator_outputs` (iterator box, no `ref`/`fn`), or\n  (c) `comparator` field set (comparator box, no `ref`/`fn`).\n- For `kind == \"data\"`: a `value` field; no `inputs` or `connections`\n  (other than outgoing wires from this box's output slot).\n\nBox ids must be unique across the map. Connection endpoints must\nreference valid box ids and valid input names.\n\nSchema rules mirror `src/001-schema.lua`. The C validator is a port of\nthat file's logic, simplified by the absence of port-named branching\n(removed in issue 108 cleanup).\n\n### 4. Topology validation\n- Every connection's `from_box` and `to_box` exist.\n- Every connection's `to_input_name` matches a declared input on the\n  destination box.\n- No non-iterator cycles. The validator runs DFS; any cycle that does\n  not pass through an iterator box is rejected.\n- Every required input has at least one connection feeding it (or is\n  fed by a `data` box).\n\nValidation failure aborts the program with a precise error message —\nwhich box, which connection, what was wrong.\n\n### 5. Slot size class enumeration\nWalk every box and queued-input declaration to enumerate the distinct\nslot sizes the graph will need. Each unique size becomes a size class\nin the slot allocator (issue 302). Output:\n\n```c\ngraph->size_classes      = { 64, 256, 1024, 65536 };  // example\ngraph->n_size_classes    = 4;\n```\n\nThe slot allocator pre-populates each class's free list with\n`n_workers × (count of boxes whose output is this size)` slots. This\ncovers the worst case — every worker concurrently producing an output\nat this size class — without overshooting. Demand beyond this triggers\ngrowth (issue 302); the per-thread multiplier is the right ceiling for\nthe static count, while leaving headroom for iterators that allocate\nper-invocation slots.\n\n### 6. Entry-box detection\nA box is an entry box if either:\n- It has zero inputs, or\n- All of its inputs are connected only to `data` boxes (literal values\n  with no upstream computation).\n\nEntry boxes are submitted to the pool first; everything else fires from\npost-action routing in the dispatch layer.\n\nA map can have any number of entry boxes. The user lays out the\ninitial program state via `data` boxes and entry-point call boxes; the\nrunner submits all entries at once, and the graph propagates from\nthere. There is no singular `main`.\n\n### 7. Language enumeration\nCollect the distinct `lang` values across all plain call boxes. The\npool runner uses this set to decide which language specs (issue 303)\nto load and which per-worker handles to initialize.\n\nIterator and comparator boxes have no `lang` and contribute nothing\nhere.\n\n### Note on built-in primitives vs shipped libraries\n\nThere are two distinct categories of \"things the user gets out of the\nbox,\" and they live in different places:\n\n- **Dispatch-layer primitives** are graph-topology operations whose\n  semantics are routing, not data transformation. Iterator and\n  comparator are the two so far. They have no `lang` / `ref` / `fn` —\n  the dispatch layer implements their behavior directly. Splitter\n  / fan-out is already free via wire fan-out and does not need its\n  own box kind. Possible future primitives: a \"gate\" (forward only\n  when a control input is truthy), a \"merge\" (forward whichever\n  input arrives first). These are not on the roadmap; flagged here\n  so the door stays open.\n- **Shipped libraries** are data-transformation utilities — JSON\n  parse/serialize, file read/write, string concat/split, regex,\n  shell-out. These are language-specific (string semantics differ\n  between Lua, C, and Bash) and ship as `libs/<name>.<ext>` per\n  language. They are not built into the dispatch layer; they are\n  ordinary call-box source files that users wire into their maps.\n  `libs/ollama.lua` is an existing example.\n\nThe distinction matters: dispatch-layer primitives change the graph\nmodel; shipped libraries don't. A dispatch primitive can do things a\nfunction call cannot (like routing on a counter); a library is just\ncode that happens to be vendored.\n\n## Error policy\n\nAny failure in any phase aborts the program. The loader prints:\n- The map path\n- The phase that failed (parse / schema / topology / etc.)\n- The specific file or box that caused the failure\n- The parser's or validator's diagnostic message\n\nThen `exit(1)`. There is no partial-load mode.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- JSON library choice: cJSON (heaviest, easiest, well-maintained),\n  jsmn (tiny, no allocations, manual tree walking), or hand-rolled\n  (smallest dependency footprint, more code). Decision deferred to\n  implementation time.\n### String storage\n\nA \"string arena\" is a single `malloc`-backed buffer the graph loader\nuses to store every string it owns (box ids, file paths, function\nnames, branch tags) packed end-to-end. Each string is a `char *`\npointing into the arena. Allocating a string is just bumping the\narena's offset; freeing happens once when the arena is destroyed at\nthe end of the run, in a single `free(arena_buffer)`.\n\nThis is faster and simpler than calling `malloc` per string: one\n`free` for thousands of strings, no fragmentation, and lookup is\njust a pointer.\n\nThe arena starts small and grows on demand by `realloc`-ing to a\nlarger size when the current buffer fills up. Because every stored\nstring is referenced by a `char *` into the arena, a `realloc` that\nmoves the buffer would invalidate all the pointers — so the loader\neither uses a series of fixed-size chunks (a chunk list rather than a\nsingle growable buffer) or pre-sizes the arena from the file count\nto avoid mid-load realloc. Chunk-list is the standard answer.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Vendor the chosen JSON parser into `libs/json/`.\n2. Define `graph_t`, `box_t`, `connection_t`, `input_decl_t` in\n   `src/008-pool-runner.c` (or a sibling header).\n3. Implement phase 1 (directory walk) and phase 2 (parse). Smoke test:\n   load `maps/hello`, print the parsed tree.\n4. Implement phase 3 (schema validation) one rule at a time. Each\n   rule has a unit test against a malformed map fixture.\n5. Implement phase 4 (topology validation), including the cycle\n   detector. Test against `maps/branch-test` (valid) and a fixture\n   with a non-iterator cycle (invalid).\n6. Implement phase 5 (size class enumeration). Output should match\n   the box outputs declared in `maps/hello` and `maps/classify-demo`.\n7. Implement phases 6 (entry boxes) and 7 (languages). Verify against\n   known maps.\n8. Wire the loader into `src/008-pool-runner.c`'s `main` so the pool\n   runner starts by loading and validating before doing anything\n   else.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/003-loader.lua` — phase 2 loader, ported by this issue\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — phase 2 schema validator, also ported\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — pool runner that owns and uses the loader\n- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool lifecycle that\n  consumes the graph\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — slot allocator that consumes\n  the size class list\n- `issues/303-language-runtime-spec.md` — spec registry that consumes\n  the language list\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch layer that consumes\n  the box and connection arrays\n- `issues/219-map-compiler.md` — the compiler is the other consumer of\n  the same validation logic; the C loader and the compiler should\n  share validation code if possible\n\n## Implementation log\n\n### Phase 1 + 2 + early phase 3 — 2026-05-12\n\nWhat shipped:\n- `src/010-graph-loader.h` — public types and API. `graph_t` is\n  opaque; the box / connection / input declaration shapes are\n  public so the dispatch layer (issue 304) can walk them directly.\n  Routing kinds align with issue 233 — `routing_t` with `kind`\n  plus per-kind parameters, no legacy `comparand` /\n  `iterator_outputs` top-level fields.\n- `src/010-graph-loader.c` — implementation. Pipeline: open the\n  map dir, parse `meta.json` via the project JSON parser\n  (issue 314), walk every `.json` under `boxes/`, parse each into\n  a `box_t`, enforce kind-specific required fields (ref/routing\n  for call; path for data; inputs only for file_write), validate\n  id uniqueness across boxes. Errors return a malloc'd\n  `<file>:<line>: <message>` diagnostic via the `**err`\n  out-parameter; the pool runner's main is expected to print and\n  abort.\n- `tests/maps/hello/` and `tests/maps/branching/` — fixture maps\n  exercising the call/data combo, comparator routing (lt/eq/gt\n  branches all present), and iterator routing (n_outputs=3).\n- `tests/010-graph-loader-test.c` — 7 unit tests covering\n  successful loads of both fixtures, missing map directory,\n  NULL argument, unknown box kind, missing routing, and\n  duplicate box id. Malformed-shape tests use mkdtemp scratch\n  dirs so the tracked fixtures stay valid.\n- Memory model: one `json_arena_t` per loaded graph holds every\n  string and every parsed tree from every file; the box,\n  connection, and input declaration arrays are plain malloc.\n  `graph_destroy` releases all of it.\n- `.gitignore` anchored to `/maps/` so `tests/maps/` is tracked.\n- Makefile per-test dependency line for `010-graph-loader-test`\n  linking the loader and the JSON parser.\n\nVerified `make STRICT=1` builds cleanly; 33 tests across three\nsuites (slot store 12, graph loader 7, JSON 14) all pass.\n\nWhat's deferred to follow-on iterations within 305:\n- **Phase 4 — topology validation.** Connection endpoints store\n  string refs only. The next pass resolves `to_box` to integer\n  indices, verifies endpoints exist, and detects non-iterator\n  cycles via DFS.\n- **Phase 5 — slot size class enumeration.** The loader needs to\n  walk every box output and produce the distinct `cell_capacity`\n  values the slot store's allocator pre-populates.\n- **Phase 6 — entry-box detection.** A box with zero inputs or\n  with all inputs fed only by `data` boxes is an entry. The pool\n  runner spawns initial tasks for these.\n- **Phase 7 — language enumeration.** Distinct `lang` values\n  across call boxes, handed to the spec registry (issue 303).\n- The remaining routing kinds from issue 233 (randomizer,\n  weighted, distributor) — the parser currently rejects them with\n  a precise message.\n\nNone of those block 301 / 303 / 306. Topology and language\nenumeration land before 304 (the dispatch layer) since the\ndispatch action needs both.\n\n### Topology endpoint resolution — 2026-05-12\n\nAfter `load_boxes` succeeds, a `resolve_topology` pass walks every\noutgoing connection on every box and resolves the `to_box` string\nto its index in `graph->boxes`, and `to_input` to its index in\nthe target box's `inputs[]`. Both string refs are preserved on\n`connection_t` for diagnostics. Misses surface as\n`box 'X' has a connection to nonexistent box 'Y'` or\n`... nonexistent input 'Z'`. Two new fixture-based failure tests\nplus an assertion on the resolved indices in the happy-path\n`load_hello` test. The `branching` fixture grew three more box\nfiles (`small`, `exact`, `big`) so its three comparator branches\nhave real targets now.\n\nStill deferred within 305: slot size class enumeration, entry-box\ndetection, language enumeration.\n\n### Non-iterator cycle detection — 2026-05-12\n\nStandard DFS with white/gray/black coloring; the only twist is\nthat we skip outgoing edges from iterator-routing boxes, since\ncycles passing through an iterator are legitimate (the iterator's\ninput queue eventually empties and the loop terminates). Two new\nfixture-based tests cover the reject case (`a → b → a`, no\niterator) and the allowed case (`a → iter → b → a`).\n\n### Runtime attach (slot allocation + spec resolution) — 2026-05-12\n\n`graph_attach_runtime(g, slots, specs, default_cell_bytes, err)`\nwalks every box and:\n- allocates one 1-cell peek slot per declared input port via\n  `slot_alloc`, storing the slot id in `box->input_slot_ids[i]`;\n- resolves the spec for each call box by looking up `box->lang`\n  in the registry (or, as a fallback, by matching the file\n  extension of `box->ref`), storing the result on\n  `box->spec_idx`.\n\nThe graph also remembers its `map_dir` so the dispatch layer can\nresolve relative paths for data boxes and file_write boxes.\n\nWhat's still deferred:\n- **Language enumeration on the graph.** We resolve per-box but\n  don't expose the distinct set of languages a map uses, so\n  workers init every spec rather than only the ones in use.\n\n### Per-input slot modes + multi-spawn propagation — 2026-05-12\n\n`graph_attach_runtime` now picks the slot mode per input port:\n- A new BFS pass (`propagate_multi_spawn`) seeds every iterator-\n  routing call box as `multi_spawn = 1` and propagates the flag\n  forward through the connection graph. Every box reachable from\n  an iterator is now flagged.\n- For multi-spawn boxes, each input slot is allocated as a\n  16-cell pop ring. For single-spawn boxes, the legacy 1-cell\n  peek slot is used.\n- `box->input_slot_modes[]` carries the per-port mode\n  (`SLOT_MODE_PEEK` / `SLOT_MODE_POP`) so the dispatch action\n  picks the right read op.\n\nThis is the compile-time wire classification the architecture\ndoc described, with a single-step forward propagation rule. A\nproper per-wire classification (an iterator-rooted wire is\nmulti-push regardless of the immediate consumer's status) would\nallow finer-grained mode picks; the current rule is conservative\nin the right direction (slots that *could* be POP are POP).\n",

      "content":"/* src/010-graph-loader.h — C graph loader (phase 3), public API.\n *\n * What it is, in a sentence: reads a map directory off disk, parses\n * every JSON file in it, and produces an in-memory graph_t that the\n * dispatch layer (issue 304) and the pool runner (issue 301) walk\n * to drive a run.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Aligned to the unified routing schema\n * from issue 233 — every call box carries a routing.kind, and the\n * legacy `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` fields are gone. The data\n * and file_write box kinds from issue 229 are dispatch-layer\n * primitives — they have no function to invoke.\n *\n * Memory model: every string the graph_t holds (box ids, refs,\n * function names, branch tags, paths, input port names) lives in a\n * single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t. graph_destroy frees the\n * arena, the box / connection / input arrays, and the graph_t in\n * one call.\n *\n * Errors: graph_load returns NULL on failure and sets *err to a\n * malloc'd diagnostic of the form \"<file>:<line>: <message>\". The\n * caller frees *err. The hard-crash policy of the rest of phase 3\n * (issue 303) applies upstream — graph_load's caller decides\n * whether to abort or surface the error.\n *\n * What's implemented now: phases 1 (directory walk), 2 (JSON\n * parse), and the first part of 3 (per-box schema validation —\n * kind valid, id unique, kind-specific required fields present,\n * routing schema validated).\n *\n * What's deferred to follow-ons within 305:\n *  - Phase 4: topology validation. Connections currently store\n *    string refs (to_box / to_input); resolving those to integer\n *    indices, verifying both endpoints exist, and detecting\n *    non-iterator cycles all land in the next iteration.\n *  - Phase 5: slot size class enumeration.\n *  - Phase 6: entry-box detection.\n *  - Phase 7: language enumeration.\n *\n * None of those block 301 / 303 / 306 from starting.\n */\n\n#ifndef SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n#define SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\nextern \"C\" {\n#endif\n\n/* {{{ Box kinds */\ntypedef enum {\n    BOX_CALL,    /* runs a function via a language spec                */\n    BOX_READ,    /* value source — inline literal or file at `path`    */\n    BOX_WRITE,   /* file sink — writes one input, emits \"true\" downstream */\n} box_kind_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Routing kinds (issue 233 unified schema) */\ntypedef enum {\n    ROUTING_PLAIN,\n    ROUTING_COMPARATOR,\n    ROUTING_ITERATOR,\n    ROUTING_RANDOMIZER,    /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_WEIGHTED,      /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n    ROUTING_DISTRIBUTOR,   /* not yet parsed; reserved */\n} routing_kind_t;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    routing_kind_t kind;\n    int            n_outputs;   /* iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor */\n    double         comparand;   /* comparator */\n    /* Weighted routing: arena-owned double array of n_outputs\n     * entries. Normalised at runtime. NULL for other kinds. */\n    const double  *weights;\n} routing_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Input port declaration */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *name;       /* port name; arena-owned     */\n    const char *type;       /* \"string\" by convention     */\n    const char *literal;    /* NULL or arena-owned value  */\n    int         optional;   /* issue 230 optional flag    */\n} input_decl_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Outgoing connection */\n/* String refs are preserved for diagnostics; resolved integer\n * indices are filled in by the topology pass and let the dispatch\n * layer (issue 304) avoid string lookups at runtime. */\ntypedef struct {\n    const char *to_box;       /* destination box id (arena-owned)        */\n    const char *to_input;     /* destination port name                   */\n    const char *from_branch;  /* NULL for plain output; else branch name */\n    int         to_box_idx;   /* resolved index into graph->boxes        */\n    int         to_input_idx; /* resolved index into target's inputs[]   */\n} connection_t;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Box */\n/* Tagged so the forward declaration `typedef struct box box_t;` in\n * langs/lang-spec.h matches and the compile callback can accept a\n * `const box_t *` parameter. */\ntypedef struct box {\n    const char    *id;\n    box_kind_t     kind;\n\n    /* Call boxes */\n    const char    *lang;          /* \"lua\" / \"c\" / \"bash\" / NULL    */\n    const char    *ref;           /* source file (call only)        */\n    const char    *fn;            /* function name (call only)      */\n    const char    *returns;       /* declared output type: \"string\"/\"int\"/\n                                   * \"double\"/\"bool\"/\"bytes\"/\"json\"/\"void\"\n                                   * or NULL when the user hasn't said.\n                                   * Read by specs on the JSON-output\n                                   * path (issue 307 item 2). */\n    routing_t      routing;       /* call only                      */\n    int            output_capacity; /* 0 means variable-size        */\n\n    /* Per-box compile hints, optional, currently used by the C spec\n     * (issue 307). Lua / Bash boxes leave these at NULL / 0. All\n     * point into the graph's arena; no separate ownership. */\n    const char    *cflags;        /* extra flags appended to `cc`   */\n    int            n_link_libs;\n    const char   **link_libs;     /* each becomes `-l<name>`        */\n    int            n_headers;\n    const char   **headers;       /* `#include`d by generated wrappers */\n\n    /* Read boxes */\n    const char    *path;          /* file path (read only; ignored if value set) */\n    const char    *value;         /* inline literal; if set, read emits this directly */\n\n    /* Common */\n    int            n_inputs;\n    input_decl_t  *inputs;\n    int            n_connections;\n    connection_t  *connections;\n\n    /* Runtime state — populated by graph_attach_runtime, left at\n     * defaults (-1 / NULL / 0) by graph_load alone. */\n    int            spec_idx;       /* index into the spec registry; -1 if no spec  */\n    int           *input_slot_ids; /* n_inputs entries; -1 if not allocated yet    */\n    int           *input_slot_modes;/* 0 = PEEK (1-cell), 1 = POP (N-cell)         */\n    int            counter_slot_id;/* atomic-counter slot for iterator routing; -1 */\n    int            multi_spawn;    /* 1 if the box may fire many times in one run  */\n\n    /* 312 per-edge fast-path classification.\n     *\n     * One bit per input port: true iff the producer feeding that\n     * port shares this box's language. When set, the dispatch\n     * passes the slot's bytes to invoke_native as-is; when cleared\n     * the dispatch calls json_to_native first.\n     *\n     * One bit per outgoing connection (not per output port — a\n     * single output may fan to consumers of different languages):\n     * true iff the consumer on the other end of that connection\n     * shares this box's language. When set, push native bytes\n     * directly; when cleared, call native_to_json first and push\n     * JSON. */\n    int           *input_edge_native;   /* n_inputs entries, or NULL              */\n    int           *output_edge_native;  /* n_connections entries, or NULL         */\n} box_t;\n\n/* Slot mode constants used by box_t.input_slot_modes[]. */\n#define SLOT_MODE_PEEK 0\n#define SLOT_MODE_POP  1\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Graph */\ntypedef struct graph graph_t;\n\n/* Read a map directory and build the graph. Returns NULL on any\n * failure and sets *err to a malloc'd \"<file>:<line>: <message>\"\n * diagnostic. The caller frees *err. */\ngraph_t *graph_load(const char *map_dir, char **err);\n\n/* Free the graph and every byte it owns. Safe on NULL. */\nvoid     graph_destroy(graph_t *g);\n\n/* Accessors. */\nconst char  *graph_name        (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_description (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_entry_box_id(const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_map_dir     (const graph_t *g);\nint          graph_n_boxes     (const graph_t *g);\nconst box_t *graph_box         (const graph_t *g, int i);\nconst box_t *graph_box_by_id   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n\n/* Find a box's index by id; -1 if missing. */\nint          graph_box_index   (const graph_t *g, const char *id);\n\n/* Distinct language names used by call boxes in the map (filled\n * in by graph_attach_runtime). The pool's spec init can use this\n * to skip workers for specs the map doesn't actually use. */\nint          graph_n_languages (const graph_t *g);\nconst char  *graph_language    (const graph_t *g, int i);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Runtime attach (phase 5 + 7)\n *\n * Allocates one slot per input port for every box and resolves each\n * call box's language spec from the registry. After this call, the\n * dispatch layer can read inputs via `box->input_slot_ids[i]` and\n * invoke the spec via `spec_registry_at(r, box->spec_idx)`.\n *\n * Slot defaults for this iteration:\n *   - cell_capacity = `default_cell_bytes` (or 4096 if 0)\n *   - n_cells = 1 (peek mode)\n *   - flags = 0\n *\n * Iterator-fed wires and the multi-cell pop mode land in a follow-on\n * — they need compile-time wire classification (issue 305 phase 5\n * proper) that this iteration ducks. Returns 0 on success, -1 with\n * *err set on the first resolution or allocation failure. */\nstruct slot_store;        /* opaque forward decl */\nstruct spec_registry;     /* opaque forward decl */\nint graph_attach_runtime(graph_t *g,\n                         struct slot_store    *slots,\n                         struct spec_registry *specs,\n                         int                   default_cell_bytes,\n                         char                **err);\n/* }}} */\n\n#ifdef __cplusplus\n}\n#endif\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_GRAPH_LOADER_H */\n",
      "totalLines":231,
      "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/010-graph-loader.h",
      "numLines":231,
      "startLine":1
    }
  },

        "text":"`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\nIssue 305 ports the Lua graph loader to C because the phase-3 pool runner can't embed Lua as its own scripting layer — Lua appears only as a per-box language runtime. The loader is a one-shot at startup with hard-crash semantics, no partial-load.\nThe header file's \"What's deferred\" doc-block (lines 31–40) is actually out-of-date — the implementation log shows topology + cycle detection + attach-runtime already landed. So the comment lies. Whatever we work on, we should sync that block.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\nFrom the implementation log, here's what's still **deferred** within 305:\n\n1. **Phase 5 — slot size class enumeration** (proper, not the current `default_cell_bytes` shortcut). Walk every box output, collect distinct `output_capacity` values, hand them to the slot allocator.\n2. **Phase 6 — entry-box detection** as a graph-level array. Currently there's only a single `graph_entry_box_id`; the issue calls for \"any number of entry boxes\" — zero-input boxes or boxes fed only by `read`/data boxes.\n3. **Phase 7 — language enumeration on the graph.** Header has the accessor (`graph_n_languages`/`graph_language`) but the body of `graph_attach_runtime` resolves per-box without ever populating the distinct list.\n4. **Remaining routing kinds:** parse `randomizer`, `weighted`, `distributor` (currently rejected with a precise message).\n5. **Per-wire iterator-rooted classification** — the current multi-spawn BFS is conservative; a finer per-wire pass would let more wires stay 1-cell PEEK.\n6. **Stale doc comment** in `010-graph-loader.h` lines 26–40 — \"what's implemented now\" is wrong.\n\nOf these, my ordered suggestions for what to tackle:\n\n1. **Phase 6 + 7 together** — small, complementary, both walk the box array once at the end of `graph_load` / `graph_attach_runtime`, and both unblock real consumers (pool runner submitting all entry boxes; spec init skipping unused languages). Best value-per-line.\n2. **Phase 5 proper** — enumerate distinct `output_capacity` values into a `size_classes[]` on the graph; let the slot store pre-size its free lists per class instead of one `default_cell_bytes`.\n3. **Routing kinds (randomizer/weighted/distributor)** — parser-only work, the dispatch layer is the actual consumer (issue 304), so this is mostly speculative until dispatch needs them.\n4. **Per-wire classification refinement** — most lateral, most \"design\" rather than \"build.\"\n\nWhich of these would you like to take on? (And do you want to drive any of the design decisions — e.g. should entry-box detection treat a box fed only by `read` boxes as an entry, even if some of those reads point at files that don't exist yet?)"
