}\n381\t\n382\t        json_node_t *r_n = json_object_get(n, \"routing\");\n383\t        if (parse_routing(r_n, &box->routing, box->id, err) != 0) return -1;\n384\t\n385\t        json_node_t *oc_n = json_object_get(n, \"output_capacity\");\n386\t        if (oc_n && json_kind(oc_n) == JSON_NUMBER) {\n387\t            box->output_capacity = (int)json_number_value(oc_n);\n388\t        }\n389\t\n390\t        /* Declared return type. Optional; absence means \"raw bytes,\n391\t         * format up to the spec.\" Specs that care (the C spec's\n392\t         * JSON-output branch, for example) read this on the\n393\t         * output_native=0 path. */\n394\t        json_node_t *ret_n = json_object_get(n, \"returns\");\n395\t        if (ret_n && json_kind(ret_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n396\t            box->returns = json_string_value(ret_n);\n397\t        }\n398\t\n399\t        /* Per-box compile hints (issue 307 items 3+4). All optional;\n400\t         * any spec that ignores them gets the default behaviour. The\n401\t         * arena owns the strings and arrays — graph_destroy doesn't\n402\t         * free them. */\n403\t        json_node_t *cf_n = json_object_get(n, \"cflags\");\n404\t        if (cf_n && json_kind(cf_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n405\t            box->cflags = json_string_value(cf_n);\n406\t        }\n407\t        /* The pointer array is malloc'd (and freed in graph_destroy);\n408\t         * the string contents are owned by the JSON arena and stay\n409\t         * alive for the run. Same pattern as the routing weights\n410\t         * array elsewhere in this file. */\n411\t        json_node_t *ll_n = json_object_get(n, \"link_libs\");\n412\t        if (ll_n && json_kind(ll_n) == JSON_ARRAY) {\n413\t            int sz = json_array_size(ll_n);\n414\t            if (sz > 0) {\n415\t                const char **arr = malloc((size_t)sz * sizeof(*arr));\n416\t                if (!arr) {\n417\t                    *err = err_fmt(\"%s: oom for link_libs\", box->id);\n418\t                    return -1;\n419\t                }\n420\t                for (int i = 0; i < sz; i++) {\n421\t                    json_node_t *e = json_array_at(ll_n, i);\n422\t                    if (!e || json_kind(e) != JSON_STRING) {\n423\t                        free(arr);\n424\t                        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: link_libs[%d] is not a string\",\n425\t                                       box->id, i);\n426\t                        return -1;\n427\t                    }\n428\t                    arr[i] = json_string_value(e);\n429\t                }\n430\t                box->link_libs   = arr;\n431\t                box->n_link_libs = sz;\n432\t            }\n433\t        }\n434\t        json_node_t *hd_n = json_object_get(n, \"headers\");\n435\t        if (hd_n && json_kind(hd_n) == JSON_ARRAY) {\n436\t            int sz = json_array_size(hd_n);\n437\t            if (sz > 0) {\n438\t                const char **arr = malloc((size_t)sz * sizeof(*arr));\n439\t                if (!arr) {\n440\t                    *err = err_fmt(\"%s: oom for headers\", box->id);\n441\t                    return -1;\n442\t                }\n443\t                for (int i = 0; i < sz; i++) {\n444\t                    json_node_t *e = json_array_at(hd_n, i);\n445\t                    if (!e || json_kind(e) != JSON_STRING) {\n446\t                        free(arr);\n447\t                        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: headers[%d] is not a string\",\n448\t                                       box->id, i);\n449\t                        return -1;\n450\t                    }\n451\t                    arr[i] = json_string_value(e);\n452\t                }\n453\t                box->headers   = arr;\n454\t                box->n_headers = sz;\n455\t            }\n456\t        }\n457\t    } else if (box->kind == BOX_READ) {\n458\t        /* read accepts EITHER an inline `value` literal OR a `path`\n459\t         * field. value takes precedence at run time (the canvas\n460\t         * hides the path input port when value is set, per issue\n461\t         * 229). When neither is set, the box may still be valid if\n462\t         * its `path` arrives at runtime via the input wire — that's\n463\t         * checked in dispatch, not here. */\n464\t        json_node_t *val_n  = json_object_get(n, \"value\");\n465\t        json_node_t *path_n = json_object_get(n, \"path\");\n466\t        if (val_n && json_kind(val_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n467\t            box->value = json_string_value(val_n);\n468\t        }\n469\t        if (path_n && json_kind(path_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n470\t            box->path = json_string_value(path_n);\n471\t        }\n472\t    }\n473\t    /* write boxes: nothing additional beyond inputs. */\n474\t\n475\t    if (parse_inputs(json_object_get(n, \"inputs\"),\n476\t                     box, box->id, err) != 0) return -1;\n477\t    if (parse_connections(json_object_get(n, \"connections\"),\n478\t                          box, box->id, err) != 0) return -1;\n479\t\n480\t    return 0;\n481\t}\n482\t/* }}} */\n483\t\n484\t/* {{{ count_json_files_in_dir() — first pass, count .json entries */\n485\tstatic int count_json_files_in_dir(const char *dir, char **err)\n486\t{\n487\t    DIR *d = opendir(dir);\n488\t    if (!d) {\n489\t        *err = err_fmt(\"cannot open directory '%s'\", dir);\n490\t        return -1;\n491\t    }\n492\t    int n = 0;\n493\t    struct dirent *e;\n494\t    while ((e = readdir(d))) {\n495\t        if (e->d_name[0] == '.') continue;\n496\t        if (ends_with(e->d_name, \".json\")) n++;\n497\t    }\n498\t    closedir(d);\n499\t    return n;\n500\t}\n501\t/* }}} */\n502\t\n503\t/* {{{ load_meta() — parse map_dir/meta.json into the graph */\n504\tstatic int load_meta(graph_t *g, const char *map_dir, char **err)\n505\t{\n506\t    char path[4096];\n507\t    int w = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/meta.json\", map_dir);\n508\t    if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof path) {\n509\t        *err = err_fmt(\"meta.json path too long\");\n510\t        return -1;\n511\t    }\n512\t\n513\t    int err_line = 0; const char *err_msg = NULL;\n514\t    json_node_t *meta = json_parse_file(g->arena, path, &err_line, &err_msg);\n515\t    if (!meta) {\n516\t        *err = err_fmt(\"%s:%d: %s\", path, err_line, err_msg ? err_msg : \"parse error\");\n517\t        return -1;\n518\t    }\n519\t    if (json_kind(meta) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n520\t        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: top-level must be a JSON object\", path);\n521\t        return -1;\n522\t    }\n523\t\n524\t    json_node_t *name = json_object_get(meta, \"name\");\n525\t    if (!name || json_kind(name) != JSON_STRING) {\n526\t        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: missing 'name'\", path);\n527\t        return -1;\n528\t    }\n529\t    g->name = json_string_value(name);\n530\t\n531\t    json_node_t *entry = json_object_get(meta, \"entry_box_id\");\n532\t    if (entry && json_kind(entry) == JSON_STRING) {\n533\t        g->entry_box_id = json_string_value(entry);\n534\t    }\n535\t\n536\t    json_node_t *desc = json_object_get(meta, \"description\");\n537\t    if (desc && json_kind(desc) == JSON_STRING) {\n538\t        g->description = json_string_value(desc);\n539\t    }\n540\t\n541\t    return 0;\n542\t}\n543\t/* }}} */\n544\t\n545\t/* {{{ load_boxes() — walk boxes/, parse every .json into g->boxes */\n546\tstatic int load_boxes(graph_t *g, const char *map_dir, char **err)\n547\t{\n548\t    char dir[4096];\n549\t    int w = snprintf(dir, sizeof dir, \"%s/boxes\", map_dir);\n550\t    if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof dir) {\n551\t        *err = err_fmt(\"boxes path too long\");\n552\t        return -1;\n553\t    }\n554\t\n555\t    int n = count_json_files_in_dir(dir, err);\n556\t    if (n < 0) return -1;\n557\t\n558\t    g->n_boxes = n;\n559\t    if (n == 0) { g->boxes = NULL; return 0; }\n560\t    g->boxes = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(box_t));\n561\t    if (!g->boxes) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }\n562\t\n563\t    DIR *d = opendir(dir);\n564\t    if (!d) { *err = err_fmt(\"cannot open directory '%s'\", dir); return -1; }\n565\t\n566\t    int i = 0;\n567\t    struct dirent *e;\n568\t    while ((e = readdir(d))) {\n569\t        if (e->d_name[0] == '.')              continue;\n570\t        if (!ends_with(e->d_name, \".json\"))   continue;\n571\t\n572\t        char path[4096];\n573\t        int wp = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/%s\", dir, e->d_name);\n574\t        if (wp < 0 || wp >= (int)sizeof path) {\n575\t            closedir(d);\n576\t            *err = err_fmt(\"box path too long\");\n577\t            return -1;\n578\t        }\n579\t\n580\t        if (parse_box_file(g, &g->boxes[i], path, err) != 0) {\n581\t            closedir(d);\n582\t            return -1;\n583\t        }\n584\t        i++;\n585\t    }\n586\t    closedir(d);\n587\t\n588\t    /* Validate id uniqueness (O(n^2) scan; n is small). */\n589\t    for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {\n590\t        for (int k = j + 1; k < n; k++) {\n591\t            if (strcmp(g->boxes[j].id, g->boxes[k].id) == 0) {\n592\t                *err = err_fmt(\"duplicate box id '%s'\", g->boxes[j].id);\n593\t                return -1;\n594\t            }\n595\t        }\n596\t    }\n597\t\n598\t    return 0;\n599\t}\n600\t/* }}} */\n601\t\n602\t/* {{{ box_is_iterator() — true iff this is a call box whose routing\n603\t * kind cuts cycles. Cycles passing through an iterator are\n604\t * legitimate (the iterator's input queue eventually empties and\n605\t * the cycle terminates); cycles that don't are deadlocks at\n606\t * load time and must be rejected. */\n607\tstatic int box_is_iterator(const box_t *b)\n608\t{\n609\t    return b->kind == BOX_CALL && b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR;\n610\t}\n611\t/* }}} */\n612\t\n613\t/* {{{ dfs_cycle() — recursive DFS for non-iterator cycle detection */\n614\t/* colors: 0 = white (not seen), 1 = gray (on current stack),\n615\t * 2 = black (finished). Returns 0 on success, -1 if a cycle was\n616\t * found; *culprit_box is the box where the back-edge was detected. */\n617\tstatic int dfs_cycle(const graph_t *g, int box_id, char *color,\n618\t                     int *culprit_box)\n619\t{\n620\t    color[box_id] = 1;\n621\t    const box_t *src = &g->boxes[box_id];\n622\t\n623\t    /* Skip outgoing edges from iterator boxes. The iterator naturally\n624\t     * terminates on input-queue empty, so cycles that loop through\n625\t     * one are legal. Skipping is the cleanest way to express\n626\t     * \"this edge doesn't propagate cycle reachability.\" */\n627\t    if (!box_is_iterator(src)) {\n628\t        for (int i = 0; i < src->n_connections; i++) {\n629\t            int dst = src->connections[i].to_box_idx;\n630\t            if (color[dst] == 1) { *culprit_box = box_id; return -1; }\n631\t            if (color[dst] == 0) {\n632\t                if (dfs_cycle(g, dst, color, culprit_box) != 0) return -1;\n633\t            }\n634\t        }\n635\t    }\n636\t    color[box_id] = 2;\n637\t    return 0;\n638\t}\n639\t/* }}} */\n640\t\n641\t/* {{{ detect_cycles() — phase 4 part 2 */\n642\tstatic int detect_cycles(const graph_t *g, char **err)\n643\t{\n644\t    if (g->n_boxes <= 0) return 0;\n645\t    char *color = calloc((size_t)g->n_boxes, 1);\n646\t    if (!color) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }\n647\t\n648\t    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n649\t        if (color[i] != 0) continue;\n650\t        int culprit = -1;\n651\t        if (dfs_cycle(g, i, color, &culprit) != 0) {\n652\t            *err = err_fmt(\"non-iterator cycle detected (back-edge from \"\n653\t                           \"box '%s'); cycles must pass through an \"\n654\t                           \"iterator-routing box\",\n655\t                           g->boxes[culprit].id);\n656\t            free(color);\n657\t            return -1;\n658\t        }\n659\t    }\n660\t    free(color);\n661\t    return 0;\n662\t}\n663\t/* }}} */\n664\t\n665\t/* {{{ resolve_topology() — phase 4 (partial: endpoints only) */\n666\t/* Walks every outgoing connection on every box. Looks up `to_box`\n667\t * as a box id and `to_input` as one of that box's declared input\n668\t * port names; fills in the integer indices. Errors out with a\n669\t * precise message on either miss. Cycle detection lands in a\n670\t * later iteration. */\n671\tstatic int resolve_topology(graph_t *g, char **err)\n672\t{\n673\t    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n674\t        box_t *src = &g->boxes[i];\n675\t        for (int j = 0; j < src->n_connections; j++) {\n676\t            connection_t *c = &src->connections[j];\n677\t            c->to_box_idx   = -1;\n678\t            c->to_input_idx = -1;\n679\t\n680\t            int found_box = -1;\n681\t            for (int k = 0; k < g->n_boxes; k++) {\n682\t                if (strcmp(g->boxes[k].id, c->to_box) == 0) { found_box = k; break; }\n683\t            }\n684\t            if (found_box < 0) {\n685\t                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s' has a connection to nonexistent box '%s'\",\n686\t                               src->id, c->to_box);\n687\t                return -1;\n688\t            }\n689\t            c->to_box_idx = found_box;\n690\t\n691\t            const box_t *dst = &g->boxes[found_box];\n692\t            int found_in = -1;\n693\t            for (int k = 0; k < dst->n_inputs; k++) {\n694\t                if (strcmp(dst->inputs[k].name, c->to_input) == 0) {\n695\t                    found_in = k; break;\n696\t                }\n697\t            }\n698\t            if (found_in < 0) {\n699\t                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s' has a connection to box '%s' on \"\n700\t                               \"nonexistent input '%s'\",\n701\t                               src->id, dst->id, c->to_input);\n702\t                return -1;\n703\t            }\n704\t            c->to_input_idx = found_in;\n705\t        }\n706\t    }\n707\t    return 0;\n708\t}\n709\t/* }}} */\n710\t\n711\t/* {{{ graph_load() */\n712\tgraph_t *graph_load(const char *map_dir, char **err)\n713\t{\n714\t    if (err) *err = NULL;\n715\t    if (!map_dir) {\n716\t        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"graph_load: NULL map_dir\");\n717\t        return NULL;\n718\t    }\n719\t\n720\t    graph_t *g = calloc(1, sizeof *g);\n721\t    if (!g) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return NULL; }\n722\t\n723\t    g->arena = json_arena_create();\n724\t    if (!g->arena) {\n725\t        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n726\t        free(g);\n727\t        return NULL;\n728\t    }\n729\t\n730\t    g->map_dir = strdup(map_dir);\n731\t    if (!g->map_dir) {\n732\t        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n733\t        graph_destroy(g);\n734\t        return NULL;\n735\t    }\n736\t\n737\t    if (load_meta(g, map_dir, err)     != 0) { graph_destroy(g); return NULL; }\n738\t    if (load_boxes(g, map_dir, err)    != 0) { graph_destroy(g); return NULL; }\n739\t    if (resolve_topology(g, err)       != 0) { graph_destroy(g); return NULL; }\n740\t    if (detect_cycles(g, err)          != 0) { graph_destroy(g); return NULL; }\n741\t\n742\t    /* Compute the same-language fast path flag per call box (issue\n743\t     * 312). A box is \"native-eligible\" iff every adjacent call box —\n744\t     * any producer feeding its inputs AND any consumer reading its\n745\t     * output — shares the box's language. Read boxes and\n746\t     * write boxes don't constrain (they emit/consume JSON-shaped\n747\t     * bytes that any spec interprets through its bridges).\n748\t     *\n749\t     * Computed in graph_load (not graph_attach_runtime) because\n750\t     * it's purely topology-derived and doesn't need the slot\n751\t     * store or registry. The dispatch action picks\n752\t     * `spec->invoke_native` when this flag is set, falling back to\n753\t     * `invoke_json` or `invoke`. Our current specs all leave\n754\t     * invoke_native NULL so the fallback runs and behaviour is\n755\t     * unchanged — but the infrastructure is in place. */\n756\t    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n757\t        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n758\t        b->input_edge_native  = NULL;\n759\t        b->output_edge_native = NULL;\n760\t        if (b->kind != BOX_CALL || !b->lang) continue;\n761\t\n762\t        /* Allocate per-port input bits and per-connection output\n763\t         * bits. malloc rather than calloc — we fill every entry\n764\t         * explicitly below. */\n765\t        if (b->n_inputs > 0) {\n766\t            b->input_edge_native = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n767\t            if (!b->input_edge_native) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return NULL; }\n768\t            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_inputs; j++) b->input_edge_native[j] = 0;\n769\t        }\n770\t        if (b->n_connections > 0) {\n771\t            b->output_edge_native = malloc((size_t)b->n_connections * sizeof(int));\n772\t            if (!b->output_edge_native) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return NULL; }\n773\t            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) b->output_edge_native[j] = 0;\n774\t        }\n775\t\n776\t        /* Outgoing edges: for each connection, the consumer's lang\n777\t         * is native iff it's also a call box in this box's\n778\t         * language. Read / write consumers are not native\n779\t         * (they don't carry a language). */\n780\t        int all_outs_native = 1;\n781\t        for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) {\n782\t            int dst = b->connections[j].to_box_idx;\n783\t            if (dst < 0) { all_outs_native = 0; continue; }\n784\t            const box_t *c = &g->boxes[dst];\n785\t            int native = (c->kind == BOX_CALL && c->lang\n786\t                          && strcmp(c->lang, b->lang) == 0);\n787\t            b->output_edge_native[j] = native;\n788\t            if (!native) all_outs_native = 0;\n789\t        }\n790\t\n791\t        (void)all_outs_native;   /* slice 5 of 312 removed the per-box bit */\n792\t\n793\t        /* Incoming edges: for each input port, scan every producer\n794\t         * in the graph; the port is native iff at least one\n795\t         * producer feeds it AND every feeding producer shares this\n796\t         * box's language. (A mixed-language fan-in downgrades the\n797\t         * port to JSON for the whole port — the slot can carry only\n798\t         * one format, and JSON is the common denominator.) */\n799\t        for (int port = 0; port < b->n_inputs; port++) {\n800\t            int any_producer = 0;\n801\t            int all_native   = 1;\n802\t            for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes; p++) {\n803\t                const box_t *prod = &g->boxes[p];\n804\t                for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n805\t                    if (prod->connections[k].to_box_idx != i)        continue;\n806\t                    if (prod->connections[k].to_input_idx != port)   continue;\n807\t                    any_producer = 1;\n808\t                    int native = (prod->kind == BOX_CALL && prod->lang\n809\t                                  && strcmp(prod->lang, b->lang) == 0);\n810\t                    if (!native) all_native = 0;\n811\t                }\n812\t            }\n813\t            b->input_edge_native[port] = (any_producer && all_native) ? 1 : 0;\n814\t        }\n815\t    }\n816\t    return g;\n817\t}\n818\t/* }}} */\n819\t\n820\t/* {{{ graph_destroy() */\n821\tvoid graph_destroy(graph_t *g)\n822\t{\n823\t    if (!g) return;\n824\t    if (g->boxes) {\n825\t        for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n826\t            free(g->boxes[i].inputs);\n827\t            free(g->boxes[i].connections);\n828\t            free(g->boxes[i].input_slot_ids);\n829\t            free(g->boxes[i].input_slot_modes);\n830\t            free(g->boxes[i].input_edge_native);\n831\t            free(g->boxes[i].output_edge_native);\n832\t            free((double *)g->boxes[i].routing.weights);\n833\t            /* per-box compile hint pointer arrays (strings inside\n834\t             * are arena-owned; only the array itself is heap) */\n835\t            free((void *)g->boxes[i].link_libs);\n836\t            free((void *)g->boxes[i].headers);\n837\t        }\n838\t        free(g->boxes);\n839\t    }\n840\t    free(g->languages);    /* element strings live in the arena */\n841\t    free(g->map_dir);\n842\t    json_arena_destroy(g->arena);\n843\t    free(g);\n844\t}\n845\t/* }}} */\n846\t\n847\t/* {{{ Accessors */\n848\tconst char *graph_name(const graph_t *g)         { return g ? g->name : NULL; }\n849\tconst char *graph_description(const graph_t *g)  { return g ? g->description : NULL; }\n850\tconst char *graph_entry_box_id(const graph_t *g) { return g ? g->entry_box_id : NULL; }\n851\tconst char *graph_map_dir(const graph_t *g)      { return g ? g->map_dir : NULL; }\n852\tint         graph_n_boxes(const graph_t *g)      { return g ? g->n_boxes : 0; }\n853\t\n854\tconst box_t *graph_box(const graph_t *g, int i)\n855\t{\n856\t    if (!g || i < 0 || i >= g->n_boxes) return NULL;\n857\t    return &g->boxes[i];\n858\t}\n859\t\n860\tconst box_t *graph_box_by_id(const graph_t *g, const char *id)\n861\t{\n862\t    if (!g || !id) return NULL;\n863\t    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n864\t        if (strcmp(g->boxes[i].id, id) == 0) return &g->boxes[i];\n865\t    }\n866\t    return NULL;\n867\t}\n868\t\n869\tint graph_box_index(const graph_t *g, const char *id)\n870\t{\n871\t    if (!g || !id) return -1;\n872\t    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n873\t        if (strcmp(g->boxes[i].id, id) == 0) return i;\n874\t    }\n875\t    return -1;\n876\t}\n877\t\n878\tint graph_n_languages(const graph_t *g) { return g ? g->n_languages : 0; }\n879\t\n880\tconst char *graph_language(const graph_t *g, int i)\n881\t{\n882\t    if (!g || i < 0 || i >= g->n_languages) return NULL;\n883\t    return g->languages[i];\n884\t}\n885\t/* }}} */\n886\t\n887\t/* {{{ resolve_spec_for_box() — find the spec index by box->lang */\n888\t/* Returns the spec's index in the registry, or -1 if not found. */\n889\tstatic int resolve_spec_for_box(const box_t *box, spec_registry_t *r)\n890\t{\n891\t    if (!box || !r) return -1;\n892\t    if (box->kind != BOX_CALL) return -1;\n893\t    if (box->lang) {\n894\t        for (int i = 0; i < spec_registry_size(r); i++) {\n895\t            const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n896\t            if (strcmp(s->name, box->lang) == 0) return i;\n897\t        }\n898\t    }\n899\t    /* Fallback: derive from ref extension if lang isn't explicit.\n900\t     * Simple search for the last '.' and match against file_ext. */\n901\t    if (box->ref) {\n902\t        const char *dot = strrchr(box->ref, '.');\n903\t        if (dot) {\n904\t            for (int i = 0; i < spec_registry_size(r); i++) {\n905\t                const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n906\t                if (s->file_ext && strcmp(s->file_ext, dot) == 0) return i;\n907\t            }\n908\t        }\n909\t    }\n910\t    return -1;\n911\t}\n912\t/* }}} */\n913\t\n914\t/* {{{ propagate_multi_spawn() — BFS forward from iterators */\n915\t/* A box is \"multi_spawn\" if it's an iterator OR if any producer\n916\t * feeding one of its inputs is itself multi_spawn. The marker\n917\t * propagates forward through the connection graph. */\n918\t#define MULTI_SPAWN_RING_CELLS 16\n919\t\n920\tstatic void propagate_multi_spawn(graph_t *g)\n921\t{\n922\t    /* Seed: every iterator-routing call box is multi_spawn. */\n923\t    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n924\t        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n925\t        b->multi_spawn = (b->kind == BOX_CALL &&\n926\t                          b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR) ? 1 : 0;\n927\t    }\n928\t    /* Fixed-point: as long as any new box gets marked, iterate. The\n929\t     * graph is small (≤ a few hundred boxes in practice), so the\n930\t     * O(n × edges) bound is fine. */\n931\t    int changed = 1;\n932\t    while (changed) {\n933\t        changed = 0;\n934\t        for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n935\t            const box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n936\t            if (!b->multi_spawn) continue;\n937\t            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) {\n938\t                int dst = b->connections[j].to_box_idx;\n939\t                if (dst < 0) continue;\n940\t                if (!g->boxes[dst].multi_spawn) {\n941\t                    g->boxes[dst].multi_spawn = 1;\n942\t                    changed = 1;\n943\t                }\n944\t            }\n945\t        }\n946\t    }\n947\t}\n948\t/* }}} */\n949\t\n950\t/* {{{ graph_attach_runtime() — phase 5 + 7 */\n951\tint graph_attach_runtime(graph_t *g,\n952\t                         struct slot_store *slots,\n953\t                         struct spec_registry *specs,\n954\t                         int default_cell_bytes,\n955\t                         char **err)\n956\t{\n957\t    if (!g || !slots) {\n958\t        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"graph_attach_runtime: NULL graph or slots\");\n959\t        return -1;\n960\t    }\n961\t    if (default_cell_bytes <= 0) default_cell_bytes = 4096;\n962\t\n963\t    /* Mark multi-spawn boxes via forward BFS from iterators so we\n964\t     * can pick the right slot mode for each input port below. */\n965\t    propagate_multi_spawn(g);\n966\t\n967\t    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n968\t        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n969\t\n970\t        /* Allocate slots per input port. Multi-spawn boxes get\n971\t         * N-cell pop rings so producers' multiple pushes accumulate\n972\t         * and each task drains one cell. Single-spawn boxes get\n973\t         * 1-cell peek slots (the legacy fast path). */\n974\t        if (b->n_inputs > 0) {\n975\t            b->input_slot_ids   = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n976\t            b->input_slot_modes = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n977\t            if (!b->input_slot_ids || !b->input_slot_modes) {\n978\t                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory allocating input slots\");\n979\t                return -1;\n980\t            }\n981\t            int n_cells = b->multi_spawn ? MULTI_SPAWN_RING_CELLS : 1;\n982\t            int mode    = b->multi_spawn ? SLOT_MODE_POP : SLOT_MODE_PEEK;\n983\t            /* Multi-spawn rings tag each cell so pops serve in\n984\t             * producer-supplied order (issue 304). Iterators pass\n985\t             * their counter as the tag; non-iterator producers pass\n986\t             * 0 and effectively get FIFO ordering. */\n987\t            int base_flags = b->multi_spawn ? SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED : 0;\n988\t            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_inputs; j++) {\n989\t                /* If any producer feeding this input port declares\n990\t                 * variable-size output (output_capacity == 0), the\n991\t                 * slot needs the large-value heap path so pushes\n992\t                 * larger than default_cell_bytes succeed. Read boxes\n993\t                 * default to output_capacity 0 since they emit\n994\t                 * arbitrary file contents; a call box opts in by\n995\t                 * setting output_capacity to 0 in its JSON. Issue\n996\t                 * 302 follow-on. */\n997\t                int slot_flags = base_flags;\n998\t                for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes && !(slot_flags & SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE); p++) {\n999\t                    const box_t *prod = &g->boxes[p];\n1000\t                    for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n1001\t                        if (prod->connections[k].to_box_idx == i &&\n1002\t                            prod->connections[k].to_input_idx == j &&\n1003\t                            prod->output_capacity == 0) {\n1004\t                            slot_flags |= SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE;\n1005\t                            break;\n1006\t                        }\n1007\t                    }\n1008\t                }\n1009\t\n1010\t                /* Slice 3 of issue 312: call-box input ports become\n1011\t                 * dual-ring slots so producers can write native or\n1012\t                 * JSON per per-edge classification, and consumers\n1013\t                 * see per-cell which_ring tags. Restrictions inherited\n1014\t                 * from slice 1: DUAL_RING doesn't combine with\n1015\t                 * LARGE_VALUE or TAGGED yet, so ports requiring those\n1016\t                 * fall back to the single-ring path (mixed-format\n1017\t                 * fan-in on those ports lands in a follow-on along\n1018\t                 * with the LARGE_VALUE / TAGGED combinations). */\n1019\t                if (b->kind == BOX_CALL && b->lang &&\n1020\t                    !(slot_flags & (SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE | SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED))) {\n1021\t                    slot_flags |= SLOT_FLAG_DUAL_RING;\n1022\t                }\n1023\t\n1024\t                slot_id_t id = slot_alloc((slot_store_t *)slots,\n1025\t                                          default_cell_bytes, n_cells,\n1026\t                                          slot_flags);\n1027\t                if (id == SLOT_INVALID) {\n1028\t                    if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': failed to allocate \"\n1029\t                                            \"slot for input '%s'\",\n1030\t                                            b->id, b->inputs[j].name);\n1031\t                    return -1;\n1032\t                }\n1033\t                b->input_slot_ids[j]   = (int)id;\n1034\t                b->input_slot_modes[j] = mode;\n1035\t            }\n1036\t        }\n1037\t\n1038\t        /* Resolve the spec index for call boxes. Non-call boxes\n1039\t         * stay at -1; the dispatch layer handles them directly. */\n1040\t        b->spec_idx = -1;\n1041\t        if (b->kind == BOX_CALL && specs) {\n1042\t            b->spec_idx = resolve_spec_for_box(b, (spec_registry_t *)specs);\n1043\t            if (b->spec_idx < 0) {\n1044\t                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': no spec found for \"\n1045\t                                        \"lang='%s' / ref='%s'\",\n1046\t                                        b->id, b->lang ? b->lang : \"(null)\",\n1047\t                                        b->ref ? b->ref : \"(null)\");\n1048\t                return -1;\n1049\t            }\n1050\t        }\n1051\t\n1052\t        /* Iterator boxes need an atomic-counter slot so the dispatch\n1053\t         * layer can pick the output branch via slot_read_inc with\n1054\t         * concurrent-safe semantics. */\n1055\t        b->counter_slot_id = -1;\n1056\t        if (b->kind == BOX_CALL &&\n1057\t            (b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR   ||\n1058\t             b->routing.kind == ROUTING_RANDOMIZER ||\n1059\t             b->routing.kind == ROUTING_WEIGHTED)) {\n1060\t            slot_id_t cid = slot_alloc((slot_store_t *)slots, 0, 0,\n1061\t                                       SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER);\n1062\t            if (cid == SLOT_INVALID) {\n1063\t                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': could not allocate \"\n1064\t                                        \"atomic-counter slot\", b->id);\n1065\t                return -1;\n1066\t            }\n1067\t            b->counter_slot_id = (int)cid;\n1068\t        }\n1069\t    }\n1070\t\n1071\t    /* Enumerate distinct languages used by call boxes. Stored as\n1072\t     * a small array of arena-owned string pointers; the pool init\n1073\t     * can use it to skip specs no box in this map uses. */\n1074\t    free(g->languages);\n1075\t    g->languages   = NULL;\n1076\t    g->n_languages = 0;\n1077\t    if (g->n_boxes > 0) {\n1078\t        g->languages = calloc((size_t)g->n_boxes, sizeof(const char *));\n1079\t        if (!g->languages) {\n1080\t            if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n1081\t            return -1;\n1082\t        }\n1083\t        for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n1084\t            const box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n1085\t            if (b->kind != BOX_CALL || !b->lang) continue;\n1086\t            int seen = 0;\n1087\t            for (int k = 0; k < g->n_languages; k++) {\n1088\t                if (strcmp(g->languages[k], b->lang) == 0) { seen = 1; break; }\n1089\t            }\n1090\t            if (!seen) g->languages[g->n_languages++] = b->lang;\n1091\t        }\n1092\t    }\n1093\t    return 0;\n1094\t}\n1095\t/* }}} */\n1096\t",

      "content":"/* src/010-graph-loader.c — C graph loader, implementation.\n *\n * Pipeline: open the map directory; parse meta.json; walk every\n * .json file under boxes/; parse each box; flatten input\n * declarations and outgoing connections per box; validate\n * per-box schema.\n *\n * Memory model: a single json_arena_t owned by the graph_t holds\n * every string and every parsed JSON tree across every file in the\n * map. Box / connection / input arrays are plain malloc — fixed\n * size after the load completes. graph_destroy frees both.\n *\n * Designed in issue 305. Phases 4–7 (topology, size classes, entry\n * boxes, language enumeration) ship in follow-on iterations.\n */\n\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <dirent.h>\n#include <stdarg.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Graph struct */\nstruct graph {\n    json_arena_t *arena;\n\n    const char   *name;\n    const char   *description;\n    const char   *entry_box_id;\n    char         *map_dir;     /* malloc'd; remembered for dispatch (read boxes,\n                                 * source-file resolution). */\n\n    int           n_boxes;\n    box_t        *boxes;\n\n    int           n_languages;\n    const char  **languages;   /* arena-owned strings */\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ err_fmt() — malloc'd diagnostic string */\n__attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)))\nstatic char *err_fmt(const char *fmt, ...)\n{\n    char buf[1024];\n    va_list ap;\n    va_start(ap, fmt);\n    int n = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof buf, fmt, ap);\n    va_end(ap);\n    if (n < 0) return NULL;\n    size_t len = (size_t)n < sizeof buf ? (size_t)n : sizeof buf - 1;\n    char *out = malloc(len + 1);\n    if (!out) return NULL;\n    memcpy(out, buf, len);\n    out[len] = '\\0';\n    return out;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ ends_with() — true iff `s` ends with `suffix` */\nstatic int ends_with(const char *s, const char *suffix)\n{\n    size_t ls = strlen(s), lf = strlen(suffix);\n    if (ls < lf) return 0;\n    return memcmp(s + ls - lf, suffix, lf) == 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_routing() — translate JSON routing object into routing_t */\nstatic int parse_routing(const json_node_t *r, routing_t *out,\n                         const char *box_id, char **err)\n{\n    if (!r) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': missing 'routing' field\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (json_kind((json_node_t *)r) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': 'routing' is not an object\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    json_node_t *kind_n = json_object_get(r, \"kind\");\n    if (!kind_n || json_kind(kind_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': routing.kind missing or not a string\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    const char *kind = json_string_value(kind_n);\n\n    memset(out, 0, sizeof *out);\n\n    if (strcmp(kind, \"plain\") == 0) {\n        out->kind = ROUTING_PLAIN;\n        out->n_outputs = 1;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (strcmp(kind, \"comparator\") == 0) {\n        out->kind = ROUTING_COMPARATOR;\n        out->n_outputs = 3;\n        json_node_t *c = json_object_get(r, \"comparand\");\n        if (!c) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparator routing missing 'comparand'\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (json_kind(c) == JSON_NUMBER) {\n            out->comparand = json_number_value(c);\n        } else if (json_kind(c) == JSON_STRING) {\n            /* Issue 233 example shows comparand as a string;\n             * tolerate either form, parse the string as a double. */\n            const char *s = json_string_value(c);\n            char *endp = NULL;\n            out->comparand = strtod(s, &endp);\n            if (endp == s) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparand '%s' is not a number\", box_id, s);\n                return -1;\n            }\n        } else {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': comparand must be number or string\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (strcmp(kind, \"iterator\") == 0) {\n        out->kind = ROUTING_ITERATOR;\n        json_node_t *n = json_object_get(r, \"n_outputs\");\n        if (!n || json_kind(n) != JSON_NUMBER) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': iterator routing missing 'n_outputs'\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        out->n_outputs = (int)json_number_value(n);\n        if (out->n_outputs < 1) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': iterator n_outputs must be >= 1\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (strcmp(kind, \"randomizer\") == 0) {\n        out->kind = ROUTING_RANDOMIZER;\n        json_node_t *n = json_object_get(r, \"n_outputs\");\n        if (!n || json_kind(n) != JSON_NUMBER) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': randomizer routing missing 'n_outputs'\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        out->n_outputs = (int)json_number_value(n);\n        if (out->n_outputs < 1) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': randomizer n_outputs must be >= 1\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (strcmp(kind, \"weighted\") == 0) {\n        out->kind = ROUTING_WEIGHTED;\n        json_node_t *w = json_object_get(r, \"weights\");\n        if (!w || json_kind(w) != JSON_ARRAY) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': weighted routing missing 'weights' array\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        int n = json_array_size(w);\n        if (n < 1) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': weighted routing 'weights' must be non-empty\", box_id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        out->n_outputs = n;\n        /* The graph loader's arena is not exposed to this function;\n         * stash a heap-allocated copy and recover it in graph_destroy\n         * via a per-box free pass — wait, simpler: allocate via the\n         * arena. We'll use the JSON arena owned by the graph. The\n         * routing_t already holds a const pointer; cast away const\n         * at allocation time. */\n        /* Use plain malloc for simplicity; the per-box free in\n         * graph_destroy frees it via a new field below. To avoid\n         * widening box_t for one field, leak through the graph's\n         * arena would be neater — but the arena pointer isn't\n         * threaded through. Just malloc + free in graph_destroy.\n         *\n         * Actually the cleanest path: the JSON parse tree's array\n         * already lives in the arena. Walk it and read values\n         * directly at dispatch time. But routing_t wants double*\n         * for fast access. Compromise: copy into a malloc'd buffer\n         * here, free in graph_destroy. */\n        double *vals = malloc((size_t)n * sizeof(double));\n        if (!vals) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }\n        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n            json_node_t *e = json_array_at(w, i);\n            if (!e || json_kind(e) != JSON_NUMBER) {\n                free(vals);\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': weights[%d] is not a number\", box_id, i);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            vals[i] = json_number_value(e);\n            if (vals[i] < 0) {\n                free(vals);\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': weights[%d] is negative\", box_id, i);\n                return -1;\n            }\n        }\n        out->weights = vals;\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': unknown routing.kind '%s' \"\n                   \"(supported: plain, comparator, iterator, \"\n                   \"randomizer, weighted)\",\n                   box_id, kind);\n    return -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_inputs() — input port array */\nstatic int parse_inputs(json_node_t *node, box_t *box,\n                        const char *box_id, char **err)\n{\n    if (!node) {\n        box->n_inputs = 0;\n        box->inputs = NULL;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (json_kind(node) != JSON_ARRAY) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': 'inputs' is not an array\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    int n = json_array_size(node);\n    box->n_inputs = n;\n    if (n == 0) { box->inputs = NULL; return 0; }\n\n    box->inputs = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(input_decl_t));\n    if (!box->inputs) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        json_node_t *item = json_array_at(node, i);\n        if (!item || json_kind(item) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': input port %d is not an object\", box_id, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        json_node_t *name_n = json_object_get(item, \"name\");\n        if (!name_n || json_kind(name_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': input port %d missing 'name'\", box_id, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->inputs[i].name = json_string_value(name_n);\n\n        json_node_t *type_n = json_object_get(item, \"type\");\n        box->inputs[i].type = (type_n && json_kind(type_n) == JSON_STRING)\n                                ? json_string_value(type_n) : \"string\";\n\n        /* `value`: only string literals supported in this iteration. */\n        json_node_t *val_n = json_object_get(item, \"value\");\n        box->inputs[i].literal = (val_n && json_kind(val_n) == JSON_STRING)\n                                    ? json_string_value(val_n) : NULL;\n\n        json_node_t *opt_n = json_object_get(item, \"optional\");\n        box->inputs[i].optional = (opt_n && json_kind(opt_n) == JSON_BOOL)\n                                    ? json_bool_value(opt_n) : 0;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_connections() — outgoing connection array */\nstatic int parse_connections(json_node_t *node, box_t *box,\n                             const char *box_id, char **err)\n{\n    if (!node) {\n        box->n_connections = 0;\n        box->connections = NULL;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (json_kind(node) != JSON_ARRAY) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': 'connections' is not an array\", box_id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    int n = json_array_size(node);\n    box->n_connections = n;\n    if (n == 0) { box->connections = NULL; return 0; }\n\n    box->connections = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(connection_t));\n    if (!box->connections) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        json_node_t *c = json_array_at(node, i);\n        if (!c || json_kind(c) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': connection %d is not an object\", box_id, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        json_node_t *to_box_n   = json_object_get(c, \"to_box\");\n        json_node_t *to_input_n = json_object_get(c, \"to_input\");\n        if (!to_box_n || json_kind(to_box_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': connection %d missing 'to_box'\", box_id, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        if (!to_input_n || json_kind(to_input_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': connection %d missing 'to_input'\", box_id, i);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->connections[i].to_box   = json_string_value(to_box_n);\n        box->connections[i].to_input = json_string_value(to_input_n);\n\n        /* from_branch is optional: NULL for plain output ports, or\n         * \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\" for comparator, or branch name for\n         * iterator. The validation that the branch matches the\n         * routing kind lives in phase 4 (topology). */\n        json_node_t *fb = json_object_get(c, \"from_branch\");\n        box->connections[i].from_branch =\n            (fb && json_kind(fb) == JSON_STRING) ? json_string_value(fb) : NULL;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ parse_box_file() — read one boxes/<id>.json into a box_t */\nstatic int parse_box_file(graph_t *g, box_t *box,\n                          const char *path, char **err)\n{\n    int err_line = 0;\n    const char *err_msg = NULL;\n    json_node_t *n = json_parse_file(g->arena, path, &err_line, &err_msg);\n    if (!n) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s:%d: %s\", path, err_line, err_msg ? err_msg : \"parse error\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (json_kind(n) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: top-level must be a JSON object\", path);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    memset(box, 0, sizeof *box);\n    box->spec_idx          = -1;   /* unresolved until graph_attach_runtime */\n    box->counter_slot_id   = -1;   /* only iterator boxes allocate one      */\n    box->multi_spawn       = 0;    /* set by graph_attach_runtime           */\n\n    /* id */\n    json_node_t *id_n = json_object_get(n, \"id\");\n    if (!id_n || json_kind(id_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: missing or non-string 'id'\", path);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    box->id = json_string_value(id_n);\n\n    /* kind */\n    json_node_t *kind_n = json_object_get(n, \"kind\");\n    if (!kind_n || json_kind(kind_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: box '%s' missing 'kind'\", path, box->id);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    const char *kind_str = json_string_value(kind_n);\n    if      (strcmp(kind_str, \"call\")  == 0) box->kind = BOX_CALL;\n    else if (strcmp(kind_str, \"read\")  == 0) box->kind = BOX_READ;\n    else if (strcmp(kind_str, \"write\") == 0) box->kind = BOX_WRITE;\n    else {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: box '%s': unknown kind '%s'\", path, box->id, kind_str);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* Kind-specific required fields */\n    if (box->kind == BOX_CALL) {\n        json_node_t *ref_n = json_object_get(n, \"ref\");\n        if (!ref_n || json_kind(ref_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"%s: call box '%s' missing 'ref'\", path, box->id);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box->ref = json_string_value(ref_n);\n\n        json_node_t *fn_n = json_object_get(n, \"fn\");\n        if (fn_n && json_kind(fn_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n            box->fn = json_string_value(fn_n);\n        }\n\n        json_node_t *lang_n = json_object_get(n, \"lang\");\n        if (lang_n && json_kind(lang_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n            box->lang = json_string_value(lang_n);\n        }\n\n        json_node_t *r_n = json_object_get(n, \"routing\");\n        if (parse_routing(r_n, &box->routing, box->id, err) != 0) return -1;\n\n        json_node_t *oc_n = json_object_get(n, \"output_capacity\");\n        if (oc_n && json_kind(oc_n) == JSON_NUMBER) {\n            box->output_capacity = (int)json_number_value(oc_n);\n        }\n\n        /* Declared return type. Optional; absence means \"raw bytes,\n         * format up to the spec.\" Specs that care (the C spec's\n         * JSON-output branch, for example) read this on the\n         * output_native=0 path. */\n        json_node_t *ret_n = json_object_get(n, \"returns\");\n        if (ret_n && json_kind(ret_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n            box->returns = json_string_value(ret_n);\n        }\n\n        /* Per-box compile hints (issue 307 items 3+4). All optional;\n         * any spec that ignores them gets the default behaviour. The\n         * arena owns the strings and arrays — graph_destroy doesn't\n         * free them. */\n        json_node_t *cf_n = json_object_get(n, \"cflags\");\n        if (cf_n && json_kind(cf_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n            box->cflags = json_string_value(cf_n);\n        }\n        /* The pointer array is malloc'd (and freed in graph_destroy);\n         * the string contents are owned by the JSON arena and stay\n         * alive for the run. Same pattern as the routing weights\n         * array elsewhere in this file. */\n        json_node_t *ll_n = json_object_get(n, \"link_libs\");\n        if (ll_n && json_kind(ll_n) == JSON_ARRAY) {\n            int sz = json_array_size(ll_n);\n            if (sz > 0) {\n                const char **arr = malloc((size_t)sz * sizeof(*arr));\n                if (!arr) {\n                    *err = err_fmt(\"%s: oom for link_libs\", box->id);\n                    return -1;\n                }\n                for (int i = 0; i < sz; i++) {\n                    json_node_t *e = json_array_at(ll_n, i);\n                    if (!e || json_kind(e) != JSON_STRING) {\n                        free(arr);\n                        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: link_libs[%d] is not a string\",\n                                       box->id, i);\n                        return -1;\n                    }\n                    arr[i] = json_string_value(e);\n                }\n                box->link_libs   = arr;\n                box->n_link_libs = sz;\n            }\n        }\n        json_node_t *hd_n = json_object_get(n, \"headers\");\n        if (hd_n && json_kind(hd_n) == JSON_ARRAY) {\n            int sz = json_array_size(hd_n);\n            if (sz > 0) {\n                const char **arr = malloc((size_t)sz * sizeof(*arr));\n                if (!arr) {\n                    *err = err_fmt(\"%s: oom for headers\", box->id);\n                    return -1;\n                }\n                for (int i = 0; i < sz; i++) {\n                    json_node_t *e = json_array_at(hd_n, i);\n                    if (!e || json_kind(e) != JSON_STRING) {\n                        free(arr);\n                        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: headers[%d] is not a string\",\n                                       box->id, i);\n                        return -1;\n                    }\n                    arr[i] = json_string_value(e);\n                }\n                box->headers   = arr;\n                box->n_headers = sz;\n            }\n        }\n    } else if (box->kind == BOX_READ) {\n        /* read accepts EITHER an inline `value` literal OR a `path`\n         * field. value takes precedence at run time (the canvas\n         * hides the path input port when value is set, per issue\n         * 229). When neither is set, the box may still be valid if\n         * its `path` arrives at runtime via the input wire — that's\n         * checked in dispatch, not here. */\n        json_node_t *val_n  = json_object_get(n, \"value\");\n        json_node_t *path_n = json_object_get(n, \"path\");\n        if (val_n && json_kind(val_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n            box->value = json_string_value(val_n);\n        }\n        if (path_n && json_kind(path_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n            box->path = json_string_value(path_n);\n        }\n    }\n    /* write boxes: nothing additional beyond inputs. */\n\n    if (parse_inputs(json_object_get(n, \"inputs\"),\n                     box, box->id, err) != 0) return -1;\n    if (parse_connections(json_object_get(n, \"connections\"),\n                          box, box->id, err) != 0) return -1;\n\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ count_json_files_in_dir() — first pass, count .json entries */\nstatic int count_json_files_in_dir(const char *dir, char **err)\n{\n    DIR *d = opendir(dir);\n    if (!d) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"cannot open directory '%s'\", dir);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    int n = 0;\n    struct dirent *e;\n    while ((e = readdir(d))) {\n        if (e->d_name[0] == '.') continue;\n        if (ends_with(e->d_name, \".json\")) n++;\n    }\n    closedir(d);\n    return n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ load_meta() — parse map_dir/meta.json into the graph */\nstatic int load_meta(graph_t *g, const char *map_dir, char **err)\n{\n    char path[4096];\n    int w = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/meta.json\", map_dir);\n    if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof path) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"meta.json path too long\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    int err_line = 0; const char *err_msg = NULL;\n    json_node_t *meta = json_parse_file(g->arena, path, &err_line, &err_msg);\n    if (!meta) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s:%d: %s\", path, err_line, err_msg ? err_msg : \"parse error\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (json_kind(meta) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: top-level must be a JSON object\", path);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    json_node_t *name = json_object_get(meta, \"name\");\n    if (!name || json_kind(name) != JSON_STRING) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"%s: missing 'name'\", path);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    g->name = json_string_value(name);\n\n    json_node_t *entry = json_object_get(meta, \"entry_box_id\");\n    if (entry && json_kind(entry) == JSON_STRING) {\n        g->entry_box_id = json_string_value(entry);\n    }\n\n    json_node_t *desc = json_object_get(meta, \"description\");\n    if (desc && json_kind(desc) == JSON_STRING) {\n        g->description = json_string_value(desc);\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ load_boxes() — walk boxes/, parse every .json into g->boxes */\nstatic int load_boxes(graph_t *g, const char *map_dir, char **err)\n{\n    char dir[4096];\n    int w = snprintf(dir, sizeof dir, \"%s/boxes\", map_dir);\n    if (w < 0 || w >= (int)sizeof dir) {\n        *err = err_fmt(\"boxes path too long\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    int n = count_json_files_in_dir(dir, err);\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n\n    g->n_boxes = n;\n    if (n == 0) { g->boxes = NULL; return 0; }\n    g->boxes = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof(box_t));\n    if (!g->boxes) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }\n\n    DIR *d = opendir(dir);\n    if (!d) { *err = err_fmt(\"cannot open directory '%s'\", dir); return -1; }\n\n    int i = 0;\n    struct dirent *e;\n    while ((e = readdir(d))) {\n        if (e->d_name[0] == '.')              continue;\n        if (!ends_with(e->d_name, \".json\"))   continue;\n\n        char path[4096];\n        int wp = snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/%s\", dir, e->d_name);\n        if (wp < 0 || wp >= (int)sizeof path) {\n            closedir(d);\n            *err = err_fmt(\"box path too long\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n\n        if (parse_box_file(g, &g->boxes[i], path, err) != 0) {\n            closedir(d);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        i++;\n    }\n    closedir(d);\n\n    /* Validate id uniqueness (O(n^2) scan; n is small). */\n    for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {\n        for (int k = j + 1; k < n; k++) {\n            if (strcmp(g->boxes[j].id, g->boxes[k].id) == 0) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"duplicate box id '%s'\", g->boxes[j].id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ box_is_iterator() — true iff this is a call box whose routing\n * kind cuts cycles. Cycles passing through an iterator are\n * legitimate (the iterator's input queue eventually empties and\n * the cycle terminates); cycles that don't are deadlocks at\n * load time and must be rejected. */\nstatic int box_is_iterator(const box_t *b)\n{\n    return b->kind == BOX_CALL && b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dfs_cycle() — recursive DFS for non-iterator cycle detection */\n/* colors: 0 = white (not seen), 1 = gray (on current stack),\n * 2 = black (finished). Returns 0 on success, -1 if a cycle was\n * found; *culprit_box is the box where the back-edge was detected. */\nstatic int dfs_cycle(const graph_t *g, int box_id, char *color,\n                     int *culprit_box)\n{\n    color[box_id] = 1;\n    const box_t *src = &g->boxes[box_id];\n\n    /* Skip outgoing edges from iterator boxes. The iterator naturally\n     * terminates on input-queue empty, so cycles that loop through\n     * one are legal. Skipping is the cleanest way to express\n     * \"this edge doesn't propagate cycle reachability.\" */\n    if (!box_is_iterator(src)) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < src->n_connections; i++) {\n            int dst = src->connections[i].to_box_idx;\n            if (color[dst] == 1) { *culprit_box = box_id; return -1; }\n            if (color[dst] == 0) {\n                if (dfs_cycle(g, dst, color, culprit_box) != 0) return -1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    color[box_id] = 2;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ detect_cycles() — phase 4 part 2 */\nstatic int detect_cycles(const graph_t *g, char **err)\n{\n    if (g->n_boxes <= 0) return 0;\n    char *color = calloc((size_t)g->n_boxes, 1);\n    if (!color) { *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return -1; }\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        if (color[i] != 0) continue;\n        int culprit = -1;\n        if (dfs_cycle(g, i, color, &culprit) != 0) {\n            *err = err_fmt(\"non-iterator cycle detected (back-edge from \"\n                           \"box '%s'); cycles must pass through an \"\n                           \"iterator-routing box\",\n                           g->boxes[culprit].id);\n            free(color);\n            return -1;\n        }\n    }\n    free(color);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ resolve_topology() — phase 4 (partial: endpoints only) */\n/* Walks every outgoing connection on every box. Looks up `to_box`\n * as a box id and `to_input` as one of that box's declared input\n * port names; fills in the integer indices. Errors out with a\n * precise message on either miss. Cycle detection lands in a\n * later iteration. */\nstatic int resolve_topology(graph_t *g, char **err)\n{\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *src = &g->boxes[i];\n        for (int j = 0; j < src->n_connections; j++) {\n            connection_t *c = &src->connections[j];\n            c->to_box_idx   = -1;\n            c->to_input_idx = -1;\n\n            int found_box = -1;\n            for (int k = 0; k < g->n_boxes; k++) {\n                if (strcmp(g->boxes[k].id, c->to_box) == 0) { found_box = k; break; }\n            }\n            if (found_box < 0) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s' has a connection to nonexistent box '%s'\",\n                               src->id, c->to_box);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            c->to_box_idx = found_box;\n\n            const box_t *dst = &g->boxes[found_box];\n            int found_in = -1;\n            for (int k = 0; k < dst->n_inputs; k++) {\n                if (strcmp(dst->inputs[k].name, c->to_input) == 0) {\n                    found_in = k; break;\n                }\n            }\n            if (found_in < 0) {\n                *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s' has a connection to box '%s' on \"\n                               \"nonexistent input '%s'\",\n                               src->id, dst->id, c->to_input);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            c->to_input_idx = found_in;\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ graph_load() */\ngraph_t *graph_load(const char *map_dir, char **err)\n{\n    if (err) *err = NULL;\n    if (!map_dir) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"graph_load: NULL map_dir\");\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    graph_t *g = calloc(1, sizeof *g);\n    if (!g) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\"); return NULL; }\n\n    g->arena = json_arena_create();\n    if (!g->arena) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        free(g);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    g->map_dir = strdup(map_dir);\n    if (!g->map_dir) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n        graph_destroy(g);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    if (load_meta(g, map_dir, err)     != 0) { graph_destroy(g); return NULL; }\n    if (load_boxes(g, map_dir, err)    != 0) { graph_destroy(g); return NULL; }\n    if (resolve_topology(g, err)       != 0) { graph_destroy(g); return NULL; }\n    if (detect_cycles(g, err)          != 0) { graph_destroy(g); return NULL; }\n\n    /* Compute the same-language fast path flag per call box (issue\n     * 312). A box is \"native-eligible\" iff every adjacent call box —\n     * any producer feeding its inputs AND any consumer reading its\n     * output — shares the box's language. Read boxes and\n     * write boxes don't constrain (they emit/consume JSON-shaped\n     * bytes that any spec interprets through its bridges).\n     *\n     * Computed in graph_load (not graph_attach_runtime) because\n     * it's purely topology-derived and doesn't need the slot\n     * store or registry. The dispatch action picks\n     * `spec->invoke_native` when this flag is set, falling back to\n     * `invoke_json` or `invoke`. Our current specs all leave\n     * invoke_native NULL so the fallback runs and behaviour is\n     * unchanged — but the infrastructure is in place. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n        b->input_edge_native  = NULL;\n        b->output_edge_native = NULL;\n        if (b->kind != BOX_CALL || !b->lang) continue;\n\n        /* Allocate per-port input bits and per-connection output\n         * bits. malloc rather than calloc — we fill every entry\n         * explicitly below. */\n        if (b->n_inputs > 0) {\n            b->input_edge_native = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->input_edge_native) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return NULL; }\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_inputs; j++) b->input_edge_native[j] = 0;\n        }\n        if (b->n_connections > 0) {\n            b->output_edge_native = malloc((size_t)b->n_connections * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->output_edge_native) { if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"oom\"); return NULL; }\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) b->output_edge_native[j] = 0;\n        }\n\n        /* Outgoing edges: for each connection, the consumer's lang\n         * is native iff it's also a call box in this box's\n         * language. Read / write consumers are not native\n         * (they don't carry a language). */\n        int all_outs_native = 1;\n        for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) {\n            int dst = b->connections[j].to_box_idx;\n            if (dst < 0) { all_outs_native = 0; continue; }\n            const box_t *c = &g->boxes[dst];\n            int native = (c->kind == BOX_CALL && c->lang\n                          && strcmp(c->lang, b->lang) == 0);\n            b->output_edge_native[j] = native;\n            if (!native) all_outs_native = 0;\n        }\n\n        (void)all_outs_native;   /* slice 5 of 312 removed the per-box bit */\n\n        /* Incoming edges: for each input port, scan every producer\n         * in the graph; the port is native iff at least one\n         * producer feeds it AND every feeding producer shares this\n         * box's language. (A mixed-language fan-in downgrades the\n         * port to JSON for the whole port — the slot can carry only\n         * one format, and JSON is the common denominator.) */\n        for (int port = 0; port < b->n_inputs; port++) {\n            int any_producer = 0;\n            int all_native   = 1;\n            for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes; p++) {\n                const box_t *prod = &g->boxes[p];\n                for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                    if (prod->connections[k].to_box_idx != i)        continue;\n                    if (prod->connections[k].to_input_idx != port)   continue;\n                    any_producer = 1;\n                    int native = (prod->kind == BOX_CALL && prod->lang\n                                  && strcmp(prod->lang, b->lang) == 0);\n                    if (!native) all_native = 0;\n                }\n            }\n            b->input_edge_native[port] = (any_producer && all_native) ? 1 : 0;\n        }\n    }\n    return g;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ graph_destroy() */\nvoid graph_destroy(graph_t *g)\n{\n    if (!g) return;\n    if (g->boxes) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n            free(g->boxes[i].inputs);\n            free(g->boxes[i].connections);\n            free(g->boxes[i].input_slot_ids);\n            free(g->boxes[i].input_slot_modes);\n            free(g->boxes[i].input_edge_native);\n            free(g->boxes[i].output_edge_native);\n            free((double *)g->boxes[i].routing.weights);\n            /* per-box compile hint pointer arrays (strings inside\n             * are arena-owned; only the array itself is heap) */\n            free((void *)g->boxes[i].link_libs);\n            free((void *)g->boxes[i].headers);\n        }\n        free(g->boxes);\n    }\n    free(g->languages);    /* element strings live in the arena */\n    free(g->map_dir);\n    json_arena_destroy(g->arena);\n    free(g);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Accessors */\nconst char *graph_name(const graph_t *g)         { return g ? g->name : NULL; }\nconst char *graph_description(const graph_t *g)  { return g ? g->description : NULL; }\nconst char *graph_entry_box_id(const graph_t *g) { return g ? g->entry_box_id : NULL; }\nconst char *graph_map_dir(const graph_t *g)      { return g ? g->map_dir : NULL; }\nint         graph_n_boxes(const graph_t *g)      { return g ? g->n_boxes : 0; }\n\nconst box_t *graph_box(const graph_t *g, int i)\n{\n    if (!g || i < 0 || i >= g->n_boxes) return NULL;\n    return &g->boxes[i];\n}\n\nconst box_t *graph_box_by_id(const graph_t *g, const char *id)\n{\n    if (!g || !id) return NULL;\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(g->boxes[i].id, id) == 0) return &g->boxes[i];\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nint graph_box_index(const graph_t *g, const char *id)\n{\n    if (!g || !id) return -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        if (strcmp(g->boxes[i].id, id) == 0) return i;\n    }\n    return -1;\n}\n\nint graph_n_languages(const graph_t *g) { return g ? g->n_languages : 0; }\n\nconst char *graph_language(const graph_t *g, int i)\n{\n    if (!g || i < 0 || i >= g->n_languages) return NULL;\n    return g->languages[i];\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ resolve_spec_for_box() — find the spec index by box->lang */\n/* Returns the spec's index in the registry, or -1 if not found. */\nstatic int resolve_spec_for_box(const box_t *box, spec_registry_t *r)\n{\n    if (!box || !r) return -1;\n    if (box->kind != BOX_CALL) return -1;\n    if (box->lang) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < spec_registry_size(r); i++) {\n            const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n            if (strcmp(s->name, box->lang) == 0) return i;\n        }\n    }\n    /* Fallback: derive from ref extension if lang isn't explicit.\n     * Simple search for the last '.' and match against file_ext. */\n    if (box->ref) {\n        const char *dot = strrchr(box->ref, '.');\n        if (dot) {\n            for (int i = 0; i < spec_registry_size(r); i++) {\n                const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n                if (s->file_ext && strcmp(s->file_ext, dot) == 0) return i;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ propagate_multi_spawn() — BFS forward from iterators */\n/* A box is \"multi_spawn\" if it's an iterator OR if any producer\n * feeding one of its inputs is itself multi_spawn. The marker\n * propagates forward through the connection graph. */\n#define MULTI_SPAWN_RING_CELLS 16\n\nstatic void propagate_multi_spawn(graph_t *g)\n{\n    /* Seed: every iterator-routing call box is multi_spawn. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n        b->multi_spawn = (b->kind == BOX_CALL &&\n                          b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR) ? 1 : 0;\n    }\n    /* Fixed-point: as long as any new box gets marked, iterate. The\n     * graph is small (≤ a few hundred boxes in practice), so the\n     * O(n × edges) bound is fine. */\n    int changed = 1;\n    while (changed) {\n        changed = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n            const box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n            if (!b->multi_spawn) continue;\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_connections; j++) {\n                int dst = b->connections[j].to_box_idx;\n                if (dst < 0) continue;\n                if (!g->boxes[dst].multi_spawn) {\n                    g->boxes[dst].multi_spawn = 1;\n                    changed = 1;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ graph_attach_runtime() — phase 5 + 7 */\nint graph_attach_runtime(graph_t *g,\n                         struct slot_store *slots,\n                         struct spec_registry *specs,\n                         int default_cell_bytes,\n                         char **err)\n{\n    if (!g || !slots) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"graph_attach_runtime: NULL graph or slots\");\n        return -1;\n    }\n    if (default_cell_bytes <= 0) default_cell_bytes = 4096;\n\n    /* Mark multi-spawn boxes via forward BFS from iterators so we\n     * can pick the right slot mode for each input port below. */\n    propagate_multi_spawn(g);\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n        box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n\n        /* Allocate slots per input port. Multi-spawn boxes get\n         * N-cell pop rings so producers' multiple pushes accumulate\n         * and each task drains one cell. Single-spawn boxes get\n         * 1-cell peek slots (the legacy fast path). */\n        if (b->n_inputs > 0) {\n            b->input_slot_ids   = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            b->input_slot_modes = malloc((size_t)b->n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n            if (!b->input_slot_ids || !b->input_slot_modes) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory allocating input slots\");\n                return -1;\n            }\n            int n_cells = b->multi_spawn ? MULTI_SPAWN_RING_CELLS : 1;\n            int mode    = b->multi_spawn ? SLOT_MODE_POP : SLOT_MODE_PEEK;\n            /* Multi-spawn rings tag each cell so pops serve in\n             * producer-supplied order (issue 304). Iterators pass\n             * their counter as the tag; non-iterator producers pass\n             * 0 and effectively get FIFO ordering. */\n            int base_flags = b->multi_spawn ? SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED : 0;\n            for (int j = 0; j < b->n_inputs; j++) {\n                /* If any producer feeding this input port declares\n                 * variable-size output (output_capacity == 0), the\n                 * slot needs the large-value heap path so pushes\n                 * larger than default_cell_bytes succeed. Read boxes\n                 * default to output_capacity 0 since they emit\n                 * arbitrary file contents; a call box opts in by\n                 * setting output_capacity to 0 in its JSON. Issue\n                 * 302 follow-on. */\n                int slot_flags = base_flags;\n                for (int p = 0; p < g->n_boxes && !(slot_flags & SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE); p++) {\n                    const box_t *prod = &g->boxes[p];\n                    for (int k = 0; k < prod->n_connections; k++) {\n                        if (prod->connections[k].to_box_idx == i &&\n                            prod->connections[k].to_input_idx == j &&\n                            prod->output_capacity == 0) {\n                            slot_flags |= SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE;\n                            break;\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n\n                /* Slice 3 of issue 312: call-box input ports become\n                 * dual-ring slots so producers can write native or\n                 * JSON per per-edge classification, and consumers\n                 * see per-cell which_ring tags. Restrictions inherited\n                 * from slice 1: DUAL_RING doesn't combine with\n                 * LARGE_VALUE or TAGGED yet, so ports requiring those\n                 * fall back to the single-ring path (mixed-format\n                 * fan-in on those ports lands in a follow-on along\n                 * with the LARGE_VALUE / TAGGED combinations). */\n                if (b->kind == BOX_CALL && b->lang &&\n                    !(slot_flags & (SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE | SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED))) {\n                    slot_flags |= SLOT_FLAG_DUAL_RING;\n                }\n\n                slot_id_t id = slot_alloc((slot_store_t *)slots,\n                                          default_cell_bytes, n_cells,\n                                          slot_flags);\n                if (id == SLOT_INVALID) {\n                    if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': failed to allocate \"\n                                            \"slot for input '%s'\",\n                                            b->id, b->inputs[j].name);\n                    return -1;\n                }\n                b->input_slot_ids[j]   = (int)id;\n                b->input_slot_modes[j] = mode;\n            }\n        }\n\n        /* Resolve the spec index for call boxes. Non-call boxes\n         * stay at -1; the dispatch layer handles them directly. */\n        b->spec_idx = -1;\n        if (b->kind == BOX_CALL && specs) {\n            b->spec_idx = resolve_spec_for_box(b, (spec_registry_t *)specs);\n            if (b->spec_idx < 0) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': no spec found for \"\n                                        \"lang='%s' / ref='%s'\",\n                                        b->id, b->lang ? b->lang : \"(null)\",\n                                        b->ref ? b->ref : \"(null)\");\n                return -1;\n            }\n        }\n\n        /* Iterator boxes need an atomic-counter slot so the dispatch\n         * layer can pick the output branch via slot_read_inc with\n         * concurrent-safe semantics. */\n        b->counter_slot_id = -1;\n        if (b->kind == BOX_CALL &&\n            (b->routing.kind == ROUTING_ITERATOR   ||\n             b->routing.kind == ROUTING_RANDOMIZER ||\n             b->routing.kind == ROUTING_WEIGHTED)) {\n            slot_id_t cid = slot_alloc((slot_store_t *)slots, 0, 0,\n                                       SLOT_FLAG_ATOMIC_COUNTER);\n            if (cid == SLOT_INVALID) {\n                if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"box '%s': could not allocate \"\n                                        \"atomic-counter slot\", b->id);\n                return -1;\n            }\n            b->counter_slot_id = (int)cid;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Enumerate distinct languages used by call boxes. Stored as\n     * a small array of arena-owned string pointers; the pool init\n     * can use it to skip specs no box in this map uses. */\n    free(g->languages);\n    g->languages   = NULL;\n    g->n_languages = 0;\n    if (g->n_boxes > 0) {\n        g->languages = calloc((size_t)g->n_boxes, sizeof(const char *));\n        if (!g->languages) {\n            if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"out of memory\");\n            return -1;\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; i < g->n_boxes; i++) {\n            const box_t *b = &g->boxes[i];\n            if (b->kind != BOX_CALL || !b->lang) continue;\n            int seen = 0;\n            for (int k = 0; k < g->n_languages; k++) {\n                if (strcmp(g->languages[k], b->lang) == 0) { seen = 1; break; }\n            }\n            if (!seen) g->languages[g->n_languages++] = b->lang;\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",

We don't try to be clever here. */\nstatic int has_fixtures(void)\n{\n    struct stat st;\n    return stat(FIXTURE_DIR, &st) == 0 && S_ISDIR(st.st_mode);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_load_hello() */\nstatic int test_load_hello(void)\n{\n    char *err = NULL;\n    graph_t *g = graph_load(\"tests/maps/hello\", &err);\n    if (!g) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"      graph_load failed: %s\\n\", err ? err : \"(null)\");\n        free(err);\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    ASSERT(strcmp(graph_name(g), \"hello\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(graph_entry_box_id(g), \"greet\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(graph_description(g) != NULL);\n    ASSERT(graph_n_boxes(g) == 2);\n\n    /* greet box */\n    const box_t *greet = graph_box_by_id(g, \"greet\");\n    ASSERT(greet != NULL);\n    ASSERT(greet->kind == BOX_CALL);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->lang, \"lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->ref,  \"src/hello.lua\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->fn,   \"greet\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(greet->routing.kind == ROUTING_PLAIN);\n    ASSERT(greet->output_capacity == 256);\n    ASSERT(greet->n_inputs == 2);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(greet->inputs[0].name, \"name\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(greet->inputs[0].literal == NULL);\n---\ngreet.json\nwho.json\n---\n{\n  \"id\": \"greet\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"lang\": \"lua\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/hello.lua\",\n  \"fn\": \"greet\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"name\", \"type\": \"string\" },\n    { \"name\": \"salutation\", \"type\": \"string\", \"value\": \"Hello\", \"optional\": true }\n  ],\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"plain\" },\n  \"output_capacity\": 256,\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 300, \"y\": 100 }\n}\n{\n  \"id\": \"who\",\n  \"kind\": \"read\",\n  \"path\": \"names.txt\",\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 100, \"y\": 100 },\n  \"connections\": [\n    { \"from_box\": \"who\", \"from_branch\": null,\n      \"to_box\": \"greet\", \"to_input\": \"name\" }\n  ]\n}"

  "parentUuid":"ec3834d7-5c40-4904-89d4-89337239cc62",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "newString":"## Output: `graph_t`\n\n`graph_t` is opaque; the structs it holds (`box_t`, `connection_t`,\n`input_decl_t`, `routing_t`) are public so the dispatch layer can walk\nthem without going through accessors. Box kinds are an enum:\n`BOX_CALL` (verb — runs a function), `BOX_READ` (value source — either\nan inline `value` literal or a file at `path`), `BOX_WRITE` (file sink\n— consumes one input). Routing is a tagged union on `routing_kind_t`\n(plain / comparator / iterator / randomizer / weighted / distributor)\ncarrying the per-kind parameters in the same struct.\n\nEach connection holds both its original string endpoint refs (for\ndiagnostics) and the resolved integer indices (`to_box_idx`,\n`to_input_idx`). The topology pass fills the indices in; the dispatch\nlayer uses only the indices.\n\nThe graph also exposes:\n- `n_languages` / `languages[]` — distinct language names across call\n  boxes, filled in by `graph_attach_runtime`.\n- `entry_box_id` — single name from `meta.json` (the multi-entry set\n  described below is the work this iteration adds).\n- `map_dir` — the directory the graph was loaded from, kept so the\n  dispatch layer can resolve relative paths inside read / write boxes.\n\nStrings are owned by the graph (allocated from a single JSON arena\nattached to the graph; freed when the graph is destroyed at the end\nof the run). The box / connection / input arrays are plain malloc and\nfreed in `graph_destroy`.",
    "structuredPatch":[{
